Rest is part of the plan.", 0 items, no CTA. Saturday is the last open day of the week for the builds, and Today shows nothing to do and calls the week covered.
findings.suggestedFix: Derive the Saturday offer from the week contract: the count shortfall plus undone required labs, gates and targets. Say 'covered' only when weekContract.complete is true. Otherwise list the outstanding builds and checkpoints as the optional Saturday stack, keeping the no-debt wording.

findings.title: Week status ignores labs and checkpoints on every screen; the only lab/checkpoint check can never fire
findings.specSection: §7 week completion; §29 Week completion; §26 no contradictory systems
findings.evidence: lib/course/week-status.ts:69 `const ended = today > dates[6]`; :78 `if (ended && status === 'on-track' && ((extra.labsDone ?? 0) < labsRequired || (extra.gatesCleared ?? 0) < gatesRequired)) status = 'recoverable'`; components/use-course-day.ts:32 passes extras only for the current week (today ≤ its Sunday, so ended=false); :34 `weekProgress(i + 1, weekDates(i + 1)[6], credits.byDate).status` (Sunday as 'today', no extras); components/course/readiness-report.tsx:87 same; components/course/road-map.tsx:62 `weekProgress(w.number, today, byDate)` (no extras); lib/course/readiness.ts:148-152 consumes `lastFinishedWeek`
findings.detail: No caller ever reaches `ended` with extras. The only exception is a bug path after the course ends, where Week 1 is shown. So WeekCard reads "On track" on Saturday and Sunday with 0/2 builds and 0/3 checkpoints, with copy "Week 3: 75 of 75. On track for February 1 if this output continues." The finished-week status sent to readiness is 'on-track' (computed), so a missing build never affects the track. Even if that line were reachable, it only downgrades to 'recoverable'. WeekStatus (:33) has no 'complete' value at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `weekContract(week, asOf, state)` returning {count, labs, gates, targets, complete, status}. Status must count overdue required labs and gates (for example, Saturday or Sunday with builds outstanding is not on track). Call it with the lab and gate state for finished weeks too, and add a 'complete' state.

findings.title: Following Today exactly cannot complete Week 1: focused-route deadlock in gate-less units (cross-dimension, routing.ts)
findings.evidence: lib/course/routing.ts:131 `if (path.length && path.filter((e) => passed.has(e.id)).length / path.length >= 0.4) return true`; :148 `const pathDone = full.every((e) => passed.has(e.id))`; :154 `const ready = liveGates.length ? gatesCleared : pathDone`; :157 `const path = route === 'focused' ? full.filter((e) => !LESSON_LEVEL.includes(e.stage) || passed.has(e.id)) : full`; :218 queue iterates `s.path`; :206-207 horizon from the frontier unit
findings.detail: Simulated a learner who does every prescribed item cleanly. After 40% of w1-state-while (no gates) is passed, its route becomes 'focused' and d05-while-halve [trace] drops out of the queue, but pathDone still requires it, so the unit never becomes ready. w1-loop-control, w1-running-state, w1-mutation-references and w1-integration stay locked, and none of Week 1's 4 checkpoints is ever offered. From Oct 27 Today fills with Week-2 w2-hashing reps while still showing "Day complete" on Oct 26, 28 and 30. Week 1 ends 48/50 with gates 0/4, labs 0/2 and 47 Week-1 path reps never offered. From Nov 5 the course queue gives 0 items on training days. The same trap exists in w2-improve (o2-comp-set-trace, which blocks w2-solve-map) and w7-bst (b230-trace-inorder, which pins the frontier at week 7, so the horizon stops at week 8).
findings.suggestedFix: Compute pathDone from the route's path, or stop a focused route from dropping reps that readiness requires. Add a regression test that simulates 'do exactly what Today prescribes' through Weeks 1–2 and asserts every gate is reached.

findings.title: No single authoritative completion function: 8 day-level and 6 week-level deciders that disagree
findings.specSection: §7 one truthful definition; §26 each level derives from the one below
findings.evidence: Day: course-today.tsx:68; motivation.ts:164; week-status.ts:66,86,105,118,132-134; today-plan.ts:164 `complete: repsDone >= N`; components/progress-view.tsx:70 `streak(active, today, PLAN_DAYS)` (lib/progress-90.ts:38-47). Week: week-status.ts:71-78; readiness-report.tsx:90 `const complete = p.done >= p.target && labs.filter((x) => !x.l.optional).every((x) => x.done) && gates.every((g) => g.cleared)`; road-map.tsx:24 `if (units.length && units.every((u) => u.state === 'ready' || u.state === 'maintenance')) return 'complete'`; use-course-day.ts:34; motivation.ts:114-116; course-cards.tsx:27-35
findings.detail:
Concrete disagreements:
- prescribe() reports complete=true on every rest day and covered Saturday (N = 0), while CourseToday says not complete.
- The Road map marks a week 'Complete' once its gates are cleared (placement can clear them with a handful of reps), even with 0/75 problems and no labs. The WeekCard then says Off track.
- In Progress → Weeks so far, a week missing a lab is titled "Week 3 · Pointers + State" (not complete), yet its badge (readiness-report.tsx:97) says count-only "ON TRACK".
- The Progress page streak counts any activity on 90-day-plan working days ("working days in a row"; that calendar ends 2027-01-09). Today's streak counts met course training days. They will show different numbers.
findings.suggestedFix: Put dayContract and weekContract in lib/course as the only deciders. Rebuild WeekCard, the Road map week state, the readiness-report summaries, readiness() inputs, the streak and the flame on top of them. Remove the V1 streak from Progress or point it at trainingStreak.

findings.title: Streak, flame, celebration and milestones count reps only; the streak counts days with pending checkpoints, repairs and labs
findings.specSection: §7; §20 gamification (streak = completed required training days; milestones); principle 11
findings.evidence: lib/course/week-status.ts:105 `const met = (credits[d] ?? 0) >= dailyTarget(courseWeekOf(d))`; :118 `if (done >= target) return 'blaze'`; components/course/course-today.tsx:77-84 celebrate only `if (!complete) return false`; :93 `milestoneReached(cd.total - done, cd.total)`; :203 `{milestone && complete && (`; data/course/motivation.ts:171 `export const MILESTONES = [50, 250, 500, 750, 950]`
findings.detail: In the Week-3 scenario the streak climbs 11→15 and the flame blazes and sparks every day with labs 0/2 and checkpoints 0/3. Milestones only show on a training day whose count is met. A crossing on Saturday (where complete is always false) or on a short day is lost for good: for example 9/day Mon–Fri (45) plus 5 on Saturday crosses 50 on Saturday, and on Monday `before` is already 50. The 'first training day' milestone (spec §20) is missing from MILESTONES, although motivate('milestone') has copy for it (motivation.ts:142); motivate('milestone') is never called.
findings.suggestedFix: Base the streak's 'met', the flame blaze and the celebration on dayContract.complete. Fire milestones from a persisted 'last celebrated' marker, not from a same-day crossing gated by `complete`. Add first training day, first completed week and first clean gate.

findings.title: There is no notion of a required target problem; targets never count toward day or week completion
findings.evidence: data/course/units.ts:31-33 `targets: number[]` / `readinessTargets?: number[]` (no required flag); lib/course/week-status.ts:60 extras have no targets; components/course/readiness-report.tsx:90 complete ignores targets; lib/today-plan.ts:130 foundation filter
findings.detail: Target problems per week (computed): W2 5, W3 5, W4 3, W5 3, W6 2, W7 7, W8 4, W9 3, W10 4, W11 4, W12 8. None of them appears in any completion rule. Week 2's targets cannot be prescribed in Week 2 (phaseOfWeek(2) = 'foundation'), so a Week-2 contract that required them could never be met.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an explicit `requiredTargets` per unit or week in data, schedule them on days that are not in the foundation phase (or relax the filter for required ones), and include them in dayContract and weekContract.

findings.title: Unfinished labs disappear from Today when the week rolls over (hidden backlog)
findings.evidence: components/use-course-day.ts:28 `const labs = LABS.filter((l) => l.week === week.number)...`; components/course/course-cards.tsx:53 builds list rendered only from `labs`; :34 use-course-day.ts finished statuses ignore labs
findings.detail: From Monday of week N+1, a required Week-N lab that was not done no longer appears on Today, WeekCard or the readiness track. Only Progress → Weeks so far lists "— <lab title>" (readiness-report.tsx:103-106). Missed gates carry over through the course queue; missed labs do not.
findings.suggestedFix: Carry incomplete required labs from earlier weeks into the Today stack, labelled honestly as 'from Week N' with no-guilt copy, and into the week and readiness contract.

findings.title: No week-complete state on Today; closing the week on Saturday is never acknowledged, and the Saturday copy goes stale
findings.specSection: §7; §19 (Week complete message); §1 'Get told when the day is complete'
findings.evidence: lib/course/week-status.ts:33 `export type WeekStatus = 'on-track' | 'recoverable' | 'off-track'`; components/course/course-cards.tsx:34-35 pill shows `WEEK_STATUS_LABEL[progress.status]`; motivate('week-complete') used only at components/course/readiness-report.tsx:114; course-today.tsx:68 requires 'training'; week-status.ts:27 Saturday shortfall uses `d < date`
findings.detail: A fully finished week (75/75, both builds, every checkpoint) still reads "On track" on Today. The week-complete message appears only later, on the Progress page. On Saturday `complete` can never be true. Because optionalTarget leaves out Saturday's own credits, the header "N reps would close the week" and the line "N reps would close week W; nothing is owed." stay on screen after the learner has done those N reps. Meanwhile WeekCard flips to on-track.
findings.suggestedFix: Use weekContract.complete to add a 'Complete' state to WeekCard and fire the week-complete moment on Today, including on Saturday. Compute Saturday's remaining work from credits up to and including today.

findings.title: Today prescribes reps that never count, so finishing every listed item does not reach the target
findings.specSection: §7 'The daily target and curriculum path must agree'; §8
findings.evidence: lib/course/credit.ts:37 `const PRODUCTION: Exercise['kind'][] = ['code', 'output', 'reorder', 'explain']`; :65 `if (!PRODUCTION.includes(exercise.kind)) return false`; lib/course/routing.ts:218 pushes every unpassed path rep regardless of kind; components/use-today-plan.ts:94-95 done filtered to credited keys
findings.detail: Required unit paths contain multiple-choice reps: W2 5, W8 1, W14 7 (computed). In the simulation, the prescriptions for Oct 27 and Oct 29 each included one (o2-list-literal, o2-set-empty), so doing every item gives 9/10. In the live app the passed choice rep is neither 'done' (it earned no credit) nor still queued (it was passed). It disappears from the list and an 11th item takes its place.
findings.suggestedFix: Classify non-producing reps as OPTIONAL or RETRIEVAL (per the §8 classification) and keep them out of the required path, or label them clearly as 'does not count'. Never let an item the day's count requires be one that cannot count.

findings.title: Tests lock in the reps-only contract; the §29 daily and week completion tests are missing
findings.evidence: e2e/course.spec.ts:58-73 'ten qualifying reps complete the day' expects data-complete='true' and "10 / 10" while Week 1's 2 labs and 4 checkpoints are outstanding (:44-45); lib/capacity.test.ts:170-173 'ten reps done is “training complete”'; lib/course/motivation.test.ts:26-28; lib/course/week-status.test.ts:40-44 tests the ended-week lab/gate downgrade that no screen reaches
findings.detail: No test asserts that a day or week is not complete while a lab, gate, target or repair is pending. No test follows the Today prescription across a week, which is how the routing deadlock went unnoticed.
findings.suggestedFix:
Replace these with contract tests:
- A day is not complete with each required kind pending.
- A week is not complete without the count, each lab, each gate or each target.
- Saturday copy is checked against the contract.
- A 'follow Today for two weeks' simulation.

findings.title: Week card off-track advice is wrong on Saturday and Sunday
findings.evidence: data/course/motivation.ts:120 `` `Week ${c.week}: ${wd} of ${wt}. Behind what this week needs. The shortest way back is today's target, then Saturday. No guilt, just the next rep.` ``; components/course/course-dashboard.tsx:73 WeekCard is rendered on every day type
findings.detail: On a Sunday rest day there is no target and Saturday has already passed. On Saturday, 'then Saturday' means today. The copy points to steps that do not exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Branch the copy on the day type: on Saturday, 'today can close part of it'; on Sunday or holidays, a neutral wrap-up with no instructions.

findings.title: Contradictory rest-day copy when the streak is 0
findings.specSection: §20 planned rest protects the streak; §15 (V2) planned rest
findings.evidence: components/course/course-today.tsx:140 `'Rest protects nothing and costs nothing. Tomorrow starts fresh.'`
findings.detail: 'Rest protects nothing' contradicts the streak rule ('planned rest protects it') shown in the same component.
findings.suggestedFix: Use 'Rest costs nothing. Your plan is intact.'

findings.title: After the course ends (from Feb 1, 2027) Today falls back to Week 1
findings.evidence: components/use-course-day.ts:26 `const week = WEEK_BY_NUMBER[day.week] ?? WEEK_BY_NUMBER[1]`; data/course/calendar.ts:57 `return Math.min(COURSE_WEEKS + 1, Math.floor(days / 7) + 1)` (=15); components/course/course-dashboard.tsx:64 `Week {cd.week.number} of 14`
findings.detail: On Feb 1, 2027, the interview checkpoint day, the header reads "Week 1 of 14" and WeekCard shows Week 1's labs and gates. dailyTarget(15)=15 is still demanded on weekdays.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle week > 14 explicitly: show a post-course state and no daily target, or the Week 14 summary.

findings.title: The day-complete panel leaves out builds
findings.evidence: components/course/course-today.tsx:302-306 `{progress.done} / {progress.target}` … `{cd.gatesCleared} of {cd.weekGates.length} checkpoints cleared`
findings.detail: The panel shows the week's count and checkpoints, but not the week's required labs.
findings.suggestedFix: Add 'x / y builds' from the week contract.

findings.title: Dead and misleading week data: WEEKS[].requiredLabs includes the optional Week-9 lab, and WEEKS[].gates is unused
findings.evidence: data/course/weeks.ts:57-58 `gates: units.flatMap((u) => u.gateIds)` / `requiredLabs: units.flatMap((u) => u.labIds)`; data/course/content/labs-w9w13.ts:52 `optional: true`
findings.detail: Neither field is read anywhere. Week 9 lists 2 'requiredLabs' but only 1 is required. A week contract built from this field would wrongly require the optional build.
findings.suggestedFix: Derive requiredLabs from LABS with !optional (and live gates), or remove the fields.

findings.title: Rest days still list overdue re-solves under "Outside problems today"
findings.specSection: principle 5 planned rest creates zero debt; §29 Rest
findings.evidence: components/course/course-dashboard.tsx:82-84 `<LeetcodeList items={listItems} heading="Outside problems today" />`; lib/course/resolves.ts:42 `if (due <= today && ...)`, :50 `if (nextTrainingDay(addDays(first.date, r.gap)) <= today)`
findings.detail: A re-solve due on a training day stays due on the following Sunday or holiday and shows as today's work on a rest day. It costs no count, but it reads as owed work.
findings.suggestedFix: Hide or relabel due items on rest days ('next training day').

result.summary:
The learning system in this repo is all prose and static code. I found no interactive demonstration, stepping, visualisation or diagram anywhere in it. There are 42 teaching pages (11 Week 1–2 lessons, 24 concept guides and 7 worked examples), with about 69k characters of prose (61%) and 44k characters of static code or printed output (39%). Nothing on them is visual state or an interactive demonstration. Interactivity stops at progressive reveal: the worked example's 'Next: goal N' button, the concept page's 'More examples' details block and the collapsible Learn panel. The only runnable editor ('Try it') is a non-exported component inside the rep Basics panel.

All 11 concepts in spec §14 have a concept-guide page, built from primer text, code and YouTube links. None of them has a Lesson object, a worked example or a demo. All 20 units in Weeks 3–12 have `workedExampleIds: []`. The 7 existing worked examples (Weeks 1–2) are correct but miss two of the six required phases: MANUAL REASONING and VISUAL DEMO. They also show the solution as one block with no link back to the subgoals.

The Markdown renderer supports neither tables nor ordered lists. As a result:
- the course's only state-tracing visual (the Week 1 variable table) renders as a line of pipes;
- the Week 2 Solve Map's nine steps run together as one paragraph;
- all 46 lab build/change specs run together the same way.

The pieces needed to build a demo engine exist but need extending:
- `highlightPython` uses lezer and can be split into lines, but `CodeView` has no line highlighting or line numbers.
- Motion tokens, keyframes and a global reduced-motion CSS switch exist, but there is no reduced-motion hook in JavaScript.
- The Pyodide runner exists.
- `node:test` runs only `*.test.ts` files under `lib/` and `supabase/`.
- Design tokens such as `--learn` and `--cold` are available.

I verified two things directly. All 42 lesson programs print exactly their declared output under python3. Every worked-example solution passes the examples stated in its problem. No script or test enforces either check.

The 'data' field contains the full inventory and a concrete demo architecture that fits this codebase.
result.data:
1) HOW MUCH OF THE LEARNING EXPERIENCE IS PROSE + STATIC CODE (computed with tsx over LESSONS, WORKED_EXAMPLES and CONCEPTS, counting what each component renders) - 42 teaching pages: 11 lessons (/learn/l-*), 24 concept guides (/learn/), 7 worked examples (/example/we-*). - Prose: 68,958 chars (60.8%). Static code and 'Prints' output: 44,384 chars (39.2%). Interactive or visual demonstration: 0 chars, 0 elements (0%). - About 549 prose blocks and 383 code blocks. No SVG, image, diagram or step control on any learning page. `

| pass | price | total | |---|---|---| ...

`; - the Solve Map becomes `

1. Contract: ... 9. Verify: ...

`; - 48 course rep prompts (46 lab parts plus c2-solve-plan and c2-solve-restock) contain numbered lists that collapse the same way. 6) PROPOSED REUSABLE DEMO ARCHITECTURE (React 19 client components, Tailwind v4 tokens, no new dependencies; zod is already present) Files: - `lib/demos/types.ts`: types only, no React. - `lib/demos/anchors.ts`: resolves `#@name` line anchors in demo code and strips them for display. - `lib/demos/player.ts`: pure player reducer. - `lib/demos/layout.ts`: deterministic tree and graph layout. - `lib/demos/registry.ts` - `lib/demos/{two-pointers,sliding-window,binary-search,linked-list,recursion,tree,bfs,graph,backtracking,dp,heap,intervals,trace-table}.ts`, each with a sibling `*.test.ts`. These must live in `lib/` because `run-tests.mjs` only scans `lib/` and `supabase/`. - `components/visual/demo-player.tsx` ('use client'): DemoControl plus AnimationTimeline. - `components/visual/code-trace.tsx`: CodeHighlight. - `components/visual/state-panel.tsx` - `components/visual/prediction-prompt.tsx` - `components/visual/use-reduced-motion.ts` - `components/visual/views/{array,refs,stack,tree,graph,table,timeline}.tsx`: DataStructureView. Data model (`lib/demos/types.ts`, JSON-serialisable only): ```ts type DemoValue = number | string | boolean | null | DemoValue[] | { [k: string]: DemoValue } type Tone = 'active' | 'left' | 'right' | 'window' | 'eliminated' | 'found' | 'invalid' | 'memo' | 'visited' | 'frontier' | 'undo' type DemoView = | { kind: 'array'; values: DemoValue[]; pointers: { name: string; index: number; tone: Tone }[]; regions: { from: number; to: number; tone: Tone; label?: string }[]; compare?: [number, number] } | { kind: 'refs'; objects: { id: string; label: string; next?: string | null }[]; names: { name: string; target: string | null }[]; changed?: string[] } // linked lists and the Week 1 references lesson | { kind: 'stack'; frames: { id: string; call: string; locals: Record; status: 'running' | 'waiting' | 'base' | 'returning'; returns?: DemoValue }[]; direction: 'down' | 'up' } | { kind: 'tree'; nodes: { id: string; label: string; x: number; depth: number; parent?: string; tone?: Tone; note?: string }[]; queue?: string[]; level?: number; path?: string[] } // binary tree, BFS, heap, backtracking decision tree, DP recursion tree | { kind: 'graph'; nodes: { id: string; label: string; x: number; y: number; tone?: Tone }[]; edges: { from: string; to: string; tone?: Tone }[]; directed: boolean; adjacency?: Record; frontier: string[]; visited: string[] } | { kind: 'table'; columns: string[]; rows: { label: string; cells: (DemoValue | null)[] }[]; active?: [number, number]; reads?: [number, number][] } // Week 1–2 trace tables, DP tables, grids | { kind: 'timeline'; intervals: { start: number; end: number; label: string; tone: Tone }[]; merged: [number, number][]; cursor?: number } | { kind: 'split'; parts: DemoView[] } // DP tree + memo table, heap tree + backing array interface Prediction { question: string; options: string[]; answer: number; reveal: string } interface DemoStep { lines: number[] // CODE: 1-based display lines phase: string // e.g. ENTER | INVALID | SHRINK | VALID | MEASURE title: string // CURRENT STEP why: string // WHY THIS STEP HAPPENS vars: Record // STATE VARIABLES view: DemoView // VISUAL STATE invariant?: string predict?: Prediction result?: DemoValue } interface DemoSpec { id: string title: string concept: string // a data/concepts.ts id code: string // real Python, with #@anchors phases: readonly string[] presets: { label: string; input: I }[] parse(text: string): { ok: true; input: I } | { ok: false; error: string } format(input: I): string pythonCall(input: I): string limits: { maxItems: number; maxSteps: number } generate(input: I): DemoStep[] } type DemoRef = { id: string; preset?: number; input?: string; caption?: string } ``` Player (`lib/demos/player.ts`, a pure reducer tested with `node:test`): - State: `{ index, playing, speed: 0.5 | 1 | 2, awaiting: number | null, answers: Record }`. - Actions: next, prev, reset, seek, play, pause, tick, speed, answer. - Rules: - next/tick stop before a step that has `predict` until it is answered; - tick on the last step stops playback; - reset returns to step 0 and clears answers; - seek clamps to the valid range. - `DemoPlayer` takes serialisable props `{ demoId, preset?, input?, compact? }` and imports the registry on the client. Next 16 serialises props across the server/client boundary, so functions cannot cross (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/server-and-client-boundary.md:160`). Server components such as LessonBody can still render it. - Autoplay uses `setTimeout` in an effect, with setState inside the callback. This satisfies react-hooks v7 without eslint-disable. - Cadence: 1600/900/450 ms per step at 0.5×/1×/2×. - Keyboard handlers sit on the player root, not on window (rep-workspace binds window keydown at line 561): ←/→ step, Space play/pause, R reset. Regions (spec §13): - VISUAL STATE: the view, a phase chip and an invariant banner. It has role=img with an aria-label from a pure `describe(view)`. - CODE: CodeTrace. STATE VARIABLES: StatePanel, which diffs against the previous step and marks changed values. Side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile. - CURRENT STEP and WHY THIS STEP HAPPENS, in an aria-live=polite region. - PredictionPrompt, shown when the player is awaiting an answer. - Controls: Reset · Prev · Play/Pause · Next · speed · timeline. The timeline is a range input with phase-coloured ticks and 'Step 7 / 23'. - 'Try another input': preset chips plus a parsed text field with an inline error. A deterministic 'shuffle' uses a seeded PRNG with a counter, never `Math.random` in render. - Inputs stay at 12 items or fewer, so there is no horizontal scroll at phone width with 16px gutters. CodeTrace: - Export `highlightPythonLines(code): ReactNode[][]` from `code-view.tsx` by splitting at the putBreak callback. - Render an `
    ` of lines with `data-active`. The active line gets a `var(--learn-soft)` background with a 2px inset `var(--learn)` and faint line numbers. - Keep `CodeView` unchanged for current callers. Views and phases for each §14 concept: - **two-pointers/pair-sum** (array): COMPARE → MOVE LEFT | MOVE RIGHT → FOUND. Discarded region is hatched. Example 'why': "nums[L]+nums[R] < target and nums[R] is the largest left, so nums[L] fits no pair". Prediction: 'Which pointer moves next?' - **sliding-window/longest-unique** (array, counts in vars): ENTER → INVALID → SHRINK → VALID → MEASURE. Incoming and outgoing values are tagged. - **binary-search/find and lower-bound** (array): lo/mid/hi with active vs eliminated regions. The banner reads 'If the answer exists, it is still inside this region.' - **linked-list/reverse** (refs): SAVE → REWIRE → ADVANCE with prev/current/next tags. The same view serves l-mutation-references ('Two names, one list'). - **recursion/call-stack** (stack): CALL (DOWN) → BASE → RETURN (UP), showing waiting callers and return values. - **tree/height and tree/bfs-levels** (tree): left call, right call, returned values, COMBINE. For BFS: a queue strip, the current level, and children being enqueued. - **graph/model-then-traverse** (graph): items → nodes, relationships → edges → adjacency list, then VISIT, NEIGHBORS, ENQUEUE/PUSH with frontier and visited. - **backtracking/subsets** (tree as a decision tree): CHOOSE → EXPLORE → UNDO → TRY NEXT, with the path in vars. - **dp/climb-stairs** (split view: tree plus table): RECURSE → DUPLICATE STATES → MEMO → LOOKUP → TABLE FILL. A persistent STATE/BASE/RECURRENCE/ORDER legend. Prediction: 'What should dp[4] become?' - **heap/top-k** (split view: tree plus backing array): PUSH → BUBBLE UP → POP → SIFT DOWN, with the banner 'the heap holds the best k so far'. - **intervals/merge** (timeline): SORT → COMPARE → MERGE (expand end) | START NEW. - **trace-table** (table): for l-state, l-while and l-manual. It replaces the broken Markdown table and the printed trace. Seven views cover all 11 concepts plus Weeks 1–2. Motion and tokens: - Pointer moves use `transform 200ms var(--ease-out)` (§21 micro range). - Region and state changes take 300–400ms. Add `--dur-state: 360ms`. - Changed values flash for 200ms. No infinite animation. - Under reduced motion: autoplay is off by default, steps swap with no transitions, and the global CSS rule already zeroes durations. Detect it with `useReducedMotion` built on `useSyncExternalStore` over `matchMedia`, with a server snapshot of false. - Colours: - `--accent`: current pointer; - `--cold`: second pointer; - `--learn-soft`: window and active line; - `--surface-2` with `--faint` hatch: eliminated; - `--pass/--pass-soft`: found or valid; - `--fail-soft`: invalid; - `--repair-soft`: undo. Determinism and tests (spec §29): - Generators are pure: no `Math.random`, no `Date`, no globals. Their output is JSON-serialisable, so server and client produce identical first frames with no hydration mismatch. - Generator tests in `lib/demos/*.test.ts`: - `deepEqual(gen(x), gen(clone(x)))`; - a JSON round-trip leaves the steps equal; - a deep-frozen input is not mutated; - the final result equals a brute-force reference on inputs from a seeded mulberry32 PRNG (seed inside the test). - Invariant tests: - BS: the target index stays within [lo, hi] at every step; - two pointers: eliminated indices never belong to a valid pair; - window: valid at every VALID and MEASURE step; - reversal: no node becomes unreachable from prev or current; - stack: depth returns to 0; - DP: every LOOKUP reads a filled entry; - heap: the heap property holds after each operation; - merged intervals: sorted and disjoint. - Bound tests: - steps ≤ `maxSteps` for every preset and at `maxItems`; - every entry in `lines` falls within the code; - phases ⊆ `spec.phases`; - `parse` rejects unsorted input (for BS and two pointers), too many items and non-numbers; - `format(parse(x))` round-trips. - Player reducer tests: - reset gives the initial state; - prev/next respect the bounds; - tick stops at the end; - the prediction gate holds; - seek clamps; - the reduced-motion initial state is not playing. - Python parity: add `verifyDemos` to `lib/content-check.ts`. It runs each spec's stripped code plus `pythonCall` on its presets through `runPythonBatch` and compares against the generator's final result. Call it from `verify-content.ts`, plus verify-pyodide for browser parity. - Playwright: - /learn/two-pointers: Next ×3 → data-step=3, then Reset → 0; - a custom input; - `emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` → no auto-advance. Integration and guardrails: - `Lesson.sections[].demo?: DemoRef`. - `ConceptSpec.demos?: DemoRef[]`, rendered first in ConceptBody as 'Watch it move'. This gives all 17 Week 3–12 concept pages a demo without new Lesson objects. - WorkedExample gains `manual`, `demo` and `subgoals[].lines` / `aside`. - `LearningUnit.demoIds`, used by the Today 'Watch it move' step (§5 #2) and the road-map unit detail. - `Exercise.demo?: DemoRef` on trace reps, offered as 'Watch it run' only after the answer. - Demos are never shown on gates, transfer reps, interview mode or Week 13 before an attempt, because demo titles name the technique. - Opening a demo from a prove-mode rep counts as help, the same as the `GUIDE_BEHAVIOUR` rule at `data/concepts.ts:308-312`. - Watching or predicting never earns reps, flame or readiness evidence (principle 11). Rollout: - **C1:** types, reducer, CodeTrace, StatePanel, ArrayView, PredictionPrompt and the reduced-motion hook, plus two-pointers, binary-search, sliding-window and trace-table. - **C2:** refs, stack, tree, graph, table/split and timeline views. - **D:** ten worked examples in this shape: PROBLEM → MANUAL (TraceTable) → SUBGOALS → DEMO → CODE (assembling CodeTrace) → RECONSTRUCTION. - w3-two-pointers, w4-windows, w5-binary-search, w5-linked-lists (rewiring), w6-recursion, w7-trees, w8-queue-bfs, w8-graphs, w11-backtracking, w11-dp; - then w9-heaps and w10-intervals. - Each gets a new from-blank reconstruction rep inserted into the unit path ahead of the drills. It must never be the unit's LeetCode target. 7) OBSERVATIONS FOR OTHER DIMENSIONS - w3-running-prefix's required path opens with the LC 121 capstone (cap-best-time-stock, d3-stock section) before any new teaching or worked example. It relies on W1 running-state. - Today's 'Learn first' strip, the only place a worked example is linked from Today, disappears after the unit's first rep (`course-today.tsx:101`, `done === 0`).
alreadyCorrect: Lesson code is truthful: all 42 lesson code blocks in `data/course/content/week1.ts` and `week2.ts` print exactly their declared `output` under python3 3.14 (I ran every one).

Worked-example solutions are correct. The 4 examples that state `f(args)` → value examples pass all 8 calls, and each reconstruction rep (stage 'reconstruct', from blank) exists and sits inside its unit's required path (enforced by `lib/course/content.test.ts:52-53`).

The Week 1–2 worked examples already follow the V2 subgoal pattern (`worked-example.tsx`): problem, then one goal at a time with fragment code, then the whole solution, then a 'Rebuild it' handoff to a blank-editor rep. Keep this and extend it; do not rebuild it.

Static Python highlighting exists, is cheap and is already in client bundles: `components/code-view.tsx` `highlightPython` via @lezer/highlight classHighlighter. Its putBreak callback (line 15) makes a line-aware CodeTrace a small change.

The Markdown-lite renderer (`components/markdown.tsx`) is safe (no HTML) and handles paragraphs, bullets, fenced code via CodeView, inline code, bold and italic. It only needs ordered lists and tables.

Concept guides exist for every §14 concept plus stacks, grids, tries, matrix and running-state (24 total). They are composed from primers, the single source of truth, and primer examples and recipes are verified against Python by `verifyPrimers` in `scripts/verify-content.ts`.

The Learn-layer behaviour rules are right and demos should reuse them (`data/concepts.ts:293-312` guideMode / GUIDE_BEHAVIOUR): open on first exposure, collapsed on drills, counts as help on prove, absent in interview.

Motion infrastructure is in place in `app/globals.css`: easing and duration tokens, rise-in, pop-in, draw and celebrate-in keyframes, and a global `prefers-reduced-motion` kill switch (lines 933-948).
Learning-semantic colour tokens are already wired into Tailwind v4 through `@theme inline`: `--learn`, `--learn-soft`, `--cold`, `--repair`, `--pass`, `--fail`, the surfaces and the lines.

A browser Python runtime (`lib/python/runner.ts`, Pyodide in a Worker with a timeout) and a 'Try it' editable runner pattern (`components/rep/basics-panel.tsx:256`) already exist and can be reused for editable input.

The test infrastructure suits deterministic step generators: `node:test` through `tsx --test` (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`) over `lib/**/*.test.ts`, plus python3 and Pyodide content verifiers that can host a demo/code parity check.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. Every cited line matches the code, and I reproduced the behaviour end to end.

- lib/solve-log.ts:12 is exactly `export type SolveResult = 'unaided' | 'hinted' | 'failed'`. No value means "saw the solution".
- On Today, the course dashboard (components/course/course-dashboard.tsx:83) renders `<LeetcodeList items={listItems} heading="Outside problems today" />`. That list has only two result buttons: Unaided at leetcode-list.tsx:136-138 and "Needed help" at :139-141, which calls `set(i, 'hinted')` with `aria-pressed={r === 'hinted' || r === 'failed'}`.
- The Walkthrough link (:131-135) is a plain `<a href={i.video} target="_blank">` and records nothing. In-app capstones do record it: rep-workspace.tsx:610-615 `watchWalkthrough` sets `persist({ ...a, solutionViewed: true, ... })`.
- Only two components ever write solve entries: leetcode-list.tsx (via `set`) and solve-log-view.tsx (the /log form, options at :196-200). So 'failed' can only come from /log.
- Credit: credit.ts:105-107 skips only entries with `e.result === 'failed'` and pushes `'outside-unaided' : 'outside-hinted'` for the rest. use-credits.ts feeds that into `cd.doneToday` (use-course-day.ts:35,51), and that drives `complete = day.type === 'training' && done >= target` (course-today.tsx:68). So both Today buttons produce a full qualifying credit. The existing test lib/course/credit.test.ts:46-54 asserts this, and I ran it: it passes.
- The failed-to-hinted path: in `set` (leetcode-list.tsx:50-55), a prev result of 'failed' is not equal to 'hinted', so the code saves `{...prev, result: 'hinted'}` instead of toggling the entry off.
- I simulated the flow in a scratch script that imports the real `dailyCredits`. Needed help gives ['1:outside-hinted']. Changing it to Failed in /log gives []. Tapping the already-highlighted "Needed help" again gives 'hinted', credited. Failed plus rebuilt gives [].
- The step text for new problems is real: how() at :35 returns 'New · attempt for up to 30 min, then study'. Of 188 plan LeetCode items, 176 have a walkthrough video.

Severity stays major. §10 is the V2.1 "FIX 3" requirement, and the code materially fails its "at minimum, distinguish a small hint from material solution exposure" clause. The consequence, full daily credit for solution exposure while the same panel says "Not finished yet", also touches principles 6 and 12. But that part is the §10 credit-rule finding. As stated (evidence-model granularity plus Today's two buttons), the rubric's "materially fails a V2.1 requirement" fits.
result.correctedDetail:
The claim is accurate. Two precision notes and some supporting facts.

**Precision notes**
1. The spec asks for four minimum distinctions. Two of them do exist in the data. "Rebuild from blank" is the `rebuilt?: boolean` field (lib/solve-log.ts:29), toggled at leetcode-list.tsx:155. "Later cold solve" is the review1/review2/review3/redo kinds (solve-log.ts:38). The only distinction missing from the model is small hint vs material solution exposure, which matches the claim's headline.
2. "All stored as 'hinted'" holds for Today, where Needed help is the only help option. On /log a learner can choose 'Failed', which earns no credit. The Result select is not gated by `!editing` (solve-log-view.tsx:185-202), so a Today entry can be changed there too. There is still no 'solution viewed' value.

**Supporting facts the claim omits**
- **The UI contradicts the credit.** leetcode-list.tsx:148-152 shows "Not finished yet: rebuild it…" for hinted or failed new problems. Meanwhile credit.ts:105-107 gives 'hinted' a full credit toward `cd.doneToday` and "Day complete" (course-today.tsx:68).
- **No reconstruction credit.** `dailyCredits` ignores `rebuilt`. A 'failed' entry later marked rebuilt still earns nothing, and a 'hinted' entry earns full credit without a rebuild. The spec's ladder ("solution viewed: no credit; plus rebuild: reconstruction credit") does not exist. The rebuild toggle only appears for type 'new' items that have a target state (leetcode-list.tsx:83 and :148), never for re-solves or redos.
- **Help on outside problems isn't counted as help.** use-course-day.ts:36 counts only `'assisted' || 'reconstructed'` toward `assistedToday`. 'outside-hinted' credits are left out, so the "A lot of today needed help" Day-complete caveat (data/course/motivation.ts:89-91) never accounts for them.
- **The same event gets two meanings.** /log labels an in-app capstone with `solutionViewed` as 'Failed' (solve-log-view.tsx:91). Today sends a learner who watched the walkthrough to the credited 'hinted'.
- **The toggle behaves unexpectedly.** On a 'failed' entry, "Needed help" already shows as pressed (aria-pressed is true). Tapping it does not clear the entry: it re-saves the entry as a credited 'hinted'. A second tap removes the entry.

result.summary:
Today (from Oct 26, `CourseDashboard` → `CourseToday`) is a rep counter with an ordered list of reps. It is not a daily command center. It does show the day's target and live progress, a numbered list of reps with done/now/todo states, one accent CTA, retrieval rows, rest days that create no debt, and a guilt-free "Stop for today" button. Several required pieces are missing:
- Labs never enter the ordered list.
- Checkpoints and target problems appear as steps only when the queue happens to put them in today's N items. They never show as pending or locked steps.
- Lessons and worked examples sit in a side panel under the CTA and disappear after the first rep. Interactive demos don't exist.
- There is no "Today's contract" and no "Done for today when" list.
- "Day complete · You did enough" is based on the rep count alone.

A simulation using the real lib functions found two worse problems:
- **Following Today's own list dead-ends on Day 2.** Routing's 40% "prior evidence" rule switches `w1-state-while` to a focused path that drops lesson-level reps, but readiness still requires the full path. The first unit never becomes ready and the rest of the course stays locked. The unit line keeps saying "State and while loops", and from Nov 11 Today has no list and no CTA.
- **Checkpoints come before the teaching.** For units with checkpoints, the same rule pushes the checkpoint in at 40% of the path, and 60% of the teaching is never offered.

Also:
- 55 ordinary cold/retrieval reps are labelled "Checkpoint".
- From Feb 1 2027, Today falls back to "Week 1".
- Saturday copy ignores labs and checkpoints.
- On mobile, buttons with fixed one-line text get cut off at the card edge, row titles are truncated, and tap targets are small.

All paths are under /Users/ruggudile/Desktop/Projects/reps. The throwaway scripts were deleted after use; their outputs are in the scratchpad audit folder listed in data.

findings.detail:
The rule treats the learner's own progress through a unit as 'prior evidence'. A learner who does exactly what Today lists (simulated with the real lib functions, clean first-try passes) hits this on Day 1. After 8 of 18 passes, w1-state-while switches to the focused route, which drops the unpassed lesson-level reps c1-while-fill-change and d05-while-halve. With a Today session only d05-while-halve is dropped. The unit has no gate, so 'ready' needs all 18 'full' reps, and they are never offered again. The unit never becomes ready, and w1-loop-control, w1-running-state, w1-mutation-references and everything after them stay locked.

What Today shows as a result:
- The unit line says 'State and while loops' for the rest of the course. 115 of 131 steps come from other units (w2-hashing has no prerequisites).
- Week 1 ends 50/50 reps with 0 of 4 checkpoints ever shown.
- Nov 10 offers 6 items. From Nov 11 to Jan 29 the course queue is empty. Today shows '15 reps', 0/15, no list and no CTA. In the real app only warm-up and maintenance shares, at most 6 items, could fill it, so no day can complete.

For units with checkpoints, the same rule sets state to 'placement'. Verified on w1-loop-control: after 8 of 20 path passes the next four Today items are checkpoint variants, and passing them marks the unit ready with 12 of 20 path reps never offered. Today's order therefore puts the checkpoint before the teaching.

Tests miss it: routing.test.ts `through()` passes every 'full' rep, and the e2e test covers Day 1 only.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat only evidence from before the unit first started (or before COURSE_START), or an explicit placement choice, as prior evidence. Compute pathDone against the path of the route actually in use, or keep unpassed lesson-level reps in the queue. Add a test that runs prescribe(courseQueue) day by day for all 14 weeks. It should assert that the queue never empties before the course ends, that every unit eventually becomes ready, and that gates come only after the unit's path.

I ran the real modules in a throwaway script (scripts/_audit_skeptic_lchint.ts, deleted after the run). Setup: 2026-11-09, Week 3 Monday, target 15, 14 clean reps, then LC 128 marked 'Needed help'.

This breaks §10 ("Solution viewed → does not qualify yet") and principle 12. The new-problem instructions say "attempt for up to 30 min, then study" (leetcode-list.tsx:35) or "watch the explanation first" (:34), with a Walkthrough button (:131-134). Watching the solution and then tapping 'Needed help' still earns full credit.

REFUTED: the "same page says Not finished yet" part, for the course Today page.
- After the tap, use-course.ts:21 puts every 'new' entry in solvedLc, whatever its result.
- courseQueue then drops `lc:128:new` (routing.ts:225). The simulation shows the queue before as [217,242,1,49,128] and after as [217,242,1,49].
- prescribe() rebuilds the done item from doneToday without an `lc` field (today-plan.ts:110). The simulated item is `{"key":"lc:128:new","kind":"problem","done":true}`.

Other details in the claim:
- "Ticked and struck through" only applies while the day is incomplete. Once complete, the training list is hidden (course-today.tsx:252 `!complete && plan.items.length > 0`).
- The review1 credit three days later is allowed by §10 ("Later cold re-solve → strongest evidence") when unaided. The real gap is that a hinted re-solve counts the same, with no hint-severity check.
- credit.test.ts:46-54 asserts that a hinted review1 counts. §10 allows hinted work "depending on hint severity", so a fix that adds a solution-viewed result would not have to break this test. "Will break the suite" is overstated.

- Extra edge case: on an entry saved as 'failed' from /log, the button shows as pressed (`aria-pressed={r === 'hinted' || r === 'failed'}`). Tapping it saves 'hinted', which turns zero credit into one.

Already correct: 'failed' earns no credit; credit is counted once per solve id; and CreditItem evidence labels hinted work 'outside-hinted', not unaided.

Severity stays critical. The product declares "Day complete · You did enough" and advances the streak, flame, week total and milestones on a solve where the solution was viewed. That makes progress untruthful (principle 12, §10).

result.summary:
The curriculum doesn't fit the workload contract, and the routing that should deliver it stalls. I verified this two ways. First, a static count of every week from data/course and routing.unitReps. Second, a day-by-day simulation that runs the repo's own courseStatus, courseQueue, prescribe, dailyCredits, weekProgress and readiness functions, with every prescribed rep passed clean on the first try.

1. **Weeks 1 and 2 are overloaded.** Week 1 requires 65 path reps plus 8 gate passes, or 73 against 50 (1.46x). Week 2 requires 197 path reps plus 11 gate passes plus 5 LeetCode targets, or 213 against 60 (3.55x). The w2-hashing unit alone carries 125 required reps: 149 of the 162 reps in the Oct 2 module are now required path. Week 8 is also over: 84 against 75.
2. **The course falls behind and only catches up in Week 13.** Cumulative required load runs 176 reps behind the cumulative target after Week 2.
3. **Ungated units deadlock (critical).** Routing switches an ungated unit to the "focused" route after 40% of its own reps are passed. That drops the unpassed lesson-level reps from what Today offers, but the unit's ready check still requires the full path. Affected units: w1-state-while, w2-improve and w7-bst.
   - w1-state-while is a prerequisite of 30 of the 33 units.
   - Run as coded, a zero-history learner gets 50/50 and 60/60 in Weeks 1–2, then 19 credits in Week 3 and 0 after that.
   - A learner with the October sprint plus the 90-day plan through Oct 25 runs out of course work after 11 reps on Oct 27.
4. **Week 2 tests later topics.** w2-testing includes the o11-edges reps on binary search, stacks, intervals, grids and linked lists, and Today shows them as "Checkpoint" items.
5. **Placement gives up after one checkpoint.** It starts in the middle of a unit's path, and after one checkpoint attempt it sends the learner back to the rest of the path.
6. **Week 13 can't be completed from Today.** Today can prescribe at most 5 transfer reps a day (11 with warm-ups and maintenance) against 15, and Week 14 stays locked until all 48 are done.
7. **weekProgress knows nothing about paths.** Its rule that a missing lab or checkpoint downgrades the week never fires in production: on Sunday, 50/50 with 0 of 2 labs and 0 of 4 checkpoints shows "On track".
8. **Four surfaces define "week complete" differently.** These are the week card, Road to Ready, the readiness report and readiness.
9. **No exercise is classified individually.** Nothing marks a rep as required path, optional, repair inventory, retrieval, placement or stretch.

The calendar math, the exclusion of labs and gate variants from credit, and gate pool sizes are correct. I created no files in the repo; all scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ruggudile-Desktop-Projects-reps/63c3f883-21bf-4f72-bf73-894f272876ce/scratchpad/audit/ (math.ts, table.ts, w12.ts, sim.ts, deadlock.ts, placement.ts, cap.ts, leak.ts, purpose.ts, wkcheck.ts). There is a stray repo file, /Users/ruggudile/Desktop/Projects/reps/scripts/_audit_routing_sim2.ts, which another auditor created; it should be deleted.

Dependency order is enforced in the queue: locked units contribute nothing (routing.ts:210), and the prerequisite graph matches the spec's hard chain (course.test.ts:42-57).

Holiday weeks 9, 10 and 13 already get the reduced targets 60, 45 and 60 from training days, and their required load fits on paper: 58, 31 and 48. Week 13 still fails in practice because of the load cap (see findings).

- Zero history finishes Week 1 units on Nov 3 (66 reps) and Week 2 units on Nov 20, in calendar Week 4 (about 194 reps).
- The October learner finishes Week 2 units on Nov 12 (106 reps).
- Cumulative lag for zero history: 176 reps behind after Week 2, 56 after Week 8, caught up only in Week 13.

The learner is told 50 and 60 are enough while the required curriculum is not finished: the '50/50 but not done' case §8 forbids.
findings.suggestedFix:
Curate each week's required path down to its target, after allowing for gate passes and roughly 20% warm-up and maintenance.

- **Week 1:** the 42 c1 reps plus 8 gate passes, with legacy o2-loops, d3-running-state and d05-while cut to 1-2 picked reps or moved to repair inventory.
- **Week 2:** the 36 c2 reps plus 11 gate passes.
- **w2-hashing:** make it placement-first (g-hashing cold) plus retrieval for every learner. Its 125 reps become repair inventory or optional, and it should not be served in Week 1 (give it a week floor or prerequisite).

Passing it unlocks what comes next.'

The whole o11-edges section (10 retrieval/cold reps from the October interview module) is required path in Week 2. The heuristic check found 5 of them using skills the course first teaches in Weeks 3-10. o11-wt-two-sum also needs index maps from w2-hashing, which comes later in Week 2's teaching order.

Today labels these items 'Checkpoint', and they bypass the foundation-week checks cap as 'required'. In the zero-history simulation, Nov 9 prescribed 11 of these 'gate' items from w2-testing.

The same purposeOf rule labels 55 ordinary path reps as checkpoints across the course: w2-testing 10, w10-intervals 2, w12-matrix-tries 4, w14-interview 39.
findings.suggestedFix: Take o11-edges out of w2-testing and use it as Week 14 retrieval or interview inventory. Fill w2-testing with c2 testing reps on Week 1-2 skills only. Stop mapping repType cold / stage retrieval path reps to purpose 'gate'. Add a content test that no required rep in week w uses a gate or retrieval skill first owned by a later week.

findings.title: Placement starts mid-path and ends after the first checkpoint attempt, then sends the learner back to the full path
findings.specSection: §8 (gates must fit the designed workload; PLACEMENT classification), §2 principle 8
findings.evidence: lib/course/routing.ts:131 (the 40% rule counts in-unit passes); routing.ts:164 `else if (prior && liveGates.length && !liveGates.some((g) => g.attempted)) state = 'placement'`; routing.ts:212-214 placement queue = gate variants only; routing.ts:219-221 `// Gates once the path is done ... if (s.path.every((e) => passed.has(e.id)))`; docs/reps-2.md: 'Placement: earlier production evidence means the gate is offered first. Passing it skips the teaching.'
findings.detail:
Traced on w2-hashing for a zero-history learner, passing reps in queue order:

1. After 50 passes (40%) the unit becomes 'placement', and the queue holds 3 gate variants and no path reps.
2. After 1 clean variant, `g.attempted` ends placement. The unit goes back to learning/focused with 61 more path reps.
3. Only then are the remaining 2 variants offered: 114 reps in total.

That is neither placement (50 + 3) nor the full route (125 + 3).

- 'Passing it skips the teaching' is false for every gate with need >= 2 (28 of 30 gates) and for the units with two gates (w1-loop-control, w3-two-pointers, w4-windows).
- October learner on w1-loop-control: 4 placement variants become 1 + 5 path reps + 3 = 9.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the unit in placement until every live gate is cleared or a placement variant fails. Fall back to the focused path only after a failure. Judge prior evidence only from attempts before the unit started.

findings.title: Week completion: weekProgress ignores paths, its lab/checkpoint rule never fires in production, and four surfaces disagree
findings.specSection: §7 (week completion requires output, labs, checkpoints, targets), §8 acceptance, §26 (no contradictory systems)
findings.evidence: lib/course/week-status.ts:60 `weekProgress(week, today, credits, extra = {})`; :64 `const done = dates.filter((d) => d <= today).reduce((n, d) => n + (credits[d] ?? 0), 0)`; :69 `const ended = today > dates[6]`; :78 `if (ended && status === 'on-track' && ((extra.labsDone ?? 0) < labsRequired || ...)) status = 'recoverable'`; components/use-course-day.ts:32 passes the labs and gates only for the current week (today is never after Sunday); use-course-day.ts:34 and components/course/readiness-report.tsx:87 `weekProgress(i + 1, weekDates(i + 1)[6], credits.byDate)` (no extras, and today = Sunday, so ended is false); components/course/road-map.tsx:24 `if (units.length && units.every((u) => u.state === 'ready' || u.state === 'maintenance')) return 'complete'`; readiness-report.tsx:90 `const complete = p.done >= p.target && labs... && gates.every((g) => g.cleared)`; lib/course/readiness.ts:146 `const behindWeeks = frontier ? Math.max(0, week - frontier.unit.week) : 0`; components/course/course-today.tsx:68 `const complete = day.type === 'training' && done >= target`
findings.detail:
**weekProgress is path-blind.** It counts any qualifying credit from any unit, and never sees paths or targets.

**Its lab/checkpoint downgrade is dead code in production.** weekProgress(1, …) with 50/50 credits, 0/2 labs and 0/4 checkpoints returns 'on-track' on Oct 30, Oct 31 and Nov 1. Only a Monday-after call would return 'recoverable', and no caller passes extras with that date. The week card then reads 'Week 1: 50 of 50. On track for February 1 if this output continues.' (course-cards.tsx:35, motivation.ts:122).

**Four surfaces define a finished week differently:**
- The week card uses credits only.
- Road to Ready 'Complete' uses unit readiness (paths and gates) and ignores credits and labs.
- The readiness report's 'Week N complete' uses credits + labs + gates.
- Readiness counts how many weeks behind the course is from the earliest unready unit.

**The path still decides things indirectly.** Gate variants are queued only after the path (routing.ts:219-221).

**Simulation, deadlock bypassed:**
- October learner: Week 1 ends at 50/50 and 4/4 checkpoints with the week card 'On track', but Road to Ready shows it not complete (w1-integration 4/5) and readiness says 'The course is 1 week behind the calendar' (at risk).
- Zero history: 50/50 with 2/4 checkpoints, after Today said 'Day complete' every day.
- Required target problems are part of no contract; they are only queued (routing.ts:225).
findings.suggestedFix: Write one pure week-contract function covering credits, required labs, gate statuses, required targets and (after curation) the required path. Use it in the week card, Today, Road to Ready, the readiness report and readiness. Evaluate finished weeks with ended = true and pass the labs and gates for every week, not only the current one.

findings.title: Week 13's transfer bank can't be prescribed at 15 a day; Week 14 stays locked behind all 48; learners who are ahead are throttled and shown off track
findings.specSection: §8 (holiday and normal weeks must fit their targets; daily target and path must agree), §7
findings.evidence: lib/today-plan.ts:67 `export const LOAD_HEADROOM = 1.3`; today-plan.ts:120 `const fits = (c) => count < N && (c.units <= 1 || load + c.units + (N - count - 1) <= maxLoad) && ...`; today-plan.ts:171 `if (e.transfer) return 2`; data/course/units.ts:562 `sections: ['c13-transfer'],`; units.ts:576 w14-interview `prerequisites: ['w13-transfer'],` (w13-transfer is ungated, so all 48 reps must pass)
findings.detail:
Calling prescribe() with the 48-rep c13-transfer bank at N=15 gives 5 items, and 0 more once those are done. With 5 warm-ups and 5 cold reps also available it gives 11 (5 transfer + 3 + 3).

Week 13 therefore tops out at about 20 course credits (44 with full maintenance) against its 60 target. w14-interview cannot unlock for about 10 training days.

**Simulations:**
- Zero history: Week 13 18/60 and Week 14 25/75; w13-transfer never becomes ready.
- October learner, who is ahead: Weeks 11-13 at 33/75, 25/75 and 20/60 because only Week 13 transfer reps remain. Those weeks are shown 'off-track' although every offered item was done.
- Other days with only heavy or locked items also cannot be finished, e.g. Nov 26 at 5/15 and Dec 14 at 4/15 in the zero-history run.
findings.suggestedFix: Let the plan exceed the load headroom when no lighter required work exists, or count transfer reps as 1 for the cap. Make the Week 13 target agree with the bank, for example 48 transfer + 12 retrieval. Unlock Week 14 on the transfer grade rather than 48 of 48 passes.

findings.title: Week 8 exceeds its 75 target, and the course's load is front-loaded: 176 reps behind after Week 2
findings.evidence: data/course/units.ts:388 `sections: ['o7-deque', 'o7-tree-bfs', 'o7-cap-level-order']`; :404 `sections: ['o7-grids', 'o7-neighbors', 'o7-grid-bfs', 'o7-islands', 'o7-cold']`; :419 `sections: ['o8-adjacency', 'o8-dfs', 'o8-bfs', 'o8-cap-path-exists', 'o8-components', 'o8-cap-provinces']`
findings.detail:
**Week 8:** 75 path reps + 6 gate passes + 3 targets = 84 against 75. The path alone uses the whole week, leaving no room for checkpoints, warm-ups, maintenance or repairs.

**Distribution across the course:**
- Over target: Week 1 1.46x, Week 2 3.55x, Week 8 1.12x.
- Under target: Week 3 0.64x, Week 6 0.37x (28 of 75), Weeks 10-12 0.69-0.87x.

**Cumulative lag** (required load minus target): +23 after Week 1, +176 after Week 2, +149 after Week 3, +64 after Week 6, +56 after Week 8, +1 after Week 13. The total of 931 against 950 hides the imbalance.
findings.suggestedFix: Trim w8-grids and w8-graphs, for example by moving o7-islands or o8-components to optional or repair inventory. Rebalance so each week's required load is at most its target minus about 20%, and use the under-filled weeks (3, 6, 10-12) for retrieval and spaced review instead of spill-over.

[])])` with no readiness check; routing.ts:189-196 purposeOf derives purpose from stage and repType; scripts/audit-migration.ts:19-20 `type Action = 'keep' | 'move' | ... 'optional' | 'retire'` is written only to planning/reps-v2-migration.json and nothing imports it

Queue OPTIONAL when the learner is ahead, REPAIR only from gateStatus, and readinessTargets only after a readiness check.

findings.title: No test or audit checks that the curriculum fits the weekly targets; one test asserts the opposite
findings.evidence: lib/course/course.test.ts:11 asserts only the targets `[50, 60, 75, ...]`; course.test.ts:63 `assert.ok(path.length >= 20)` (requires a large path); scripts/audit-migration.ts:122-127 prints per-week 'Existing reps required' without comparing it to weekTarget (it showed Week 2 = 169 + 36 new); scripts/audit-curriculum.ts:8 audits only the October MODULES; lib/course/routing.test.ts uses `through()`, which passes full paths and never walks the queue
findings.detail:
§29 requires tests that Week 1 required work fits 50, Week 2 fits 60, each normal week fits 75 and holiday weeks fit their adjusted targets. None exist.

No test walks a learner through courseQueue to unit readiness, so the deadlock and placement bugs above are not caught either.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test computing, per week, required path + gate needs + uncovered required targets <= weekTarget(n) (with a maintenance allowance). Add a simulation test, like the one used here, in which a clean learner doing exactly Today's prescription reaches every unit's 'ready' state and every week's contract on time.

result.summary:
After Oct 26 the Progress page (components/progress-view.tsx) has one V2 block (Feb 1 readiness plus finished-week summaries, via readiness-report.tsx) on top of five V1 blocks: a stat row with the V1 streak, days practiced and LeetCode-tracker numbers, a 90-day minutes heatmap, minutes measured against the old V1 plan, the Day 30/60/90 checkpoints and the 90-day pattern readiness. A mixed weak-skills table sits below them, and the V1 progress rail in the header shows on every page.

I simulated learners who do exactly what the course asks. The V1 blocks contradict the V2 model at every level:
- **Streak:** Progress shows 1 and Today shows 26 on Nov 30, because Saturdays and Dec 26/31 count as V1 working days.
- **Patterns vs domains:** V1 shows 0/15 patterns cleared while V2 shows 10/15 domains Ready on Dec 12.
- **Checkpoints:** every V1 checkpoint row fails, including quotas of 5/12/22 mocks that the course forbids.
- **Header %:** 3% after a perfect Week 1 and 89% after finishing all 14 weeks.

The V2 parts also disagree with each other:
- **Readiness ignores four inputs:** the current week (it says 'On track: Output … where the plan needs them' next to 'Week 3 OFF TRACK 0/75'), labs, the transfer grade and mocks.
- **Week completion has three definitions:** the Plan can show 'COMPLETE 27/50' for a week that Progress shows as OFF TRACK.
- **Road map states follow the calendar:** weeks with unlocked units are badged Locked, and six weeks can be Active at once.
- **Evidence grid:** it merges independent and retrieval into 'Cold, independent', and the pass each problem is counted from depends on the order attempts load in (UUID order).

Missing from the §9 hierarchy:
- course progress
- the current week's output
- V2 training consistency
- mastery vs freshness
- labs/building
- Software Building and Applied AI/FDE readiness
- actionable weak skills

All the V2 libraries needed already exist: credits, weekProgress, trainingStreak, courseStatus, gateStatus, masteryEvidence, labProgress/aiFde, transferGrade/mockPolicy and WeekStrip. So the fix is mostly removing the V1 blocks, then routing everything through one week-completion contract and one readiness input object. No test covers /progress.
