Course reps have no calendar day, so they are always eligible, and untouched reps rank first. Across skills the first pick is a Week-13 transfer rep for 24 skills, a gate variant for 13 (c6-g-fast-slow-a, c8-g-graph-a, c10-g-interval-a), a mock problem for 11 and a lab build for 3. A gate variant attempted this way counts as a gate try: failing it marks a possibly locked unit 'gate-blocked' with a focused route, and passing it clears gates without the path. Week-13 problems get used up before Week 13.
findings.suggestedFix: Filter cold (and prep) candidates in useTodayPlan to reps of ready, maintenance or in-progress unlocked units (UNIT_OF_EXERCISE plus statuses). Exclude GATE_OF_EXERCISE reps, lab reps, transfer and Week-13 reps, mock reps and the interview bank. Better: pass a course eligibility predicate into buildReviewSession.

findings.title: Week 1 and Week 2 required paths do not fit their contracts (73 vs 50, 208 vs 60; Week 8 81 vs 75); nothing classifies reps or tests the fit
findings.specSection: §8 FIX 1 (requirements and acceptance); §29 curriculum math; §2 principle 12
findings.evidence: data/course/units.ts:49 `sections: ['c1-state', 'c1-while', 'd05-while']`, :64 `['c1-loop-control', 'o2-loops']`, :79 `['c1-running-state', 'd3-running-state']`; units.ts:201 w2-hashing 16 sections = 125 required reps; lib/course/week-status.ts:78 a finished week missing gates becomes `'recoverable'`; lib/course/course.test.ts:11 asserts only targets `[50, 60, 75, ...]`; planning/reps-v2-migration.md:39-40 itself lists 23+42 and 169+36 required
findings.detail: Path reps plus minimum gate passes: W1 65+8=73 vs 50; W2 197+11=208 vs 60 (w2-hashing alone 125); W8 75+6=81 vs 75. Weeks 3–7 and 9–14 fit. Weeks 1–2 need 281 reps against a contract of 110, so a beginner doing exactly what is prescribed is still on Week-2 units in calendar weeks 4–5 (simulation agrees). weekProgress and WeekCard check the calendar week's gates, which the learner cannot reach yet, so every finished week is downgraded to 'recoverable' even though all prescribed work was done. This is the '50/50 but not actually done' case §8 forbids. Units have only sections/optional; there is no REQUIRED/OPTIONAL/REPAIR/RETRIEVAL/PLACEMENT/STRETCH classification, and whole legacy sections were inherited.
findings.suggestedFix: Add per-rep classification (or a curated required list) to units. Move the legacy bulk (w2-hashing's 125, o2-loops, d3-*, o11-edges) to optional, retrieval, repair or placement inventory. Add a test that required path plus gate need is at most weekTarget for every week, including holiday weeks.

findings.title: Week 2's required w2-testing path includes cold interview reps on binary search, stacks, intervals, grids and linked lists
findings.evidence: data/course/units.ts:156 `sections: ['c2-testing', 'o11-edges']`. Skills of the o11-edges reps (all stage retrieval, repType cold): o11-edge-bsearch-fix (binary_search, search_invariant), o11-wt-bsearch (search_invariant), o11-dbg-brackets (matching_pairs, stack_push_pop), o11-dbg-touching (interval_overlap, sorting), o11-dbg-empty-grid (grid_nested), o11-edge-kth-end (linked_list_traversal, two_pointer), o11-wt-two-sum (index_map, complement; w2-hashing is not a prerequisite)
findings.detail: All 10 reps must be passed before w2-testing, and therefore w2-solve-map, can complete. About 7 of them test Week 3–10 material cold, long before it is taught. purposeOf turns them into 'gate' items labelled 'Checkpoint'; in the beginner simulation one Week-2 day held 11 'Checkpoint' items.
findings.suggestedFix: Move o11-edges to w14-interview or retrieval inventory and use edge-case reps on Week 1–2 material instead. Add a content test that every required path rep's skills are taught within the unit or its prerequisite closure.

findings.title: prescribe cannot fill the day when the rest of the queue is heavy or short: Week 13 caps at 5/15, blocked-checkpoint and end-of-unit days at 3–4/15
findings.specSection: §7 truthful daily contract; §2 principles 5, 8, 13; §29 daily completion
findings.evidence: lib/today-plan.ts:67 `export const LOAD_HEADROOM = 1.3`; today-plan.ts:120 `const fits = (c: Candidate) => count < N && (c.units <= 1 || load + c.units + (N - count - 1) <= maxLoad) && ...`; today-plan.ts:171 `if (e.transfer) return 2`; data/course/units.ts:562 `sections: ['c13-transfer']` (48 transfer reps); routing.ts:210 locked dependants contribute nothing; components/course/course-today.tsx:209 a CTA only when `next` exists
findings.detail: With N=15, the load limit is 20 and every remaining item weighs 2, so at most 5 fit (2k + 15 - k <= 20). Simulated: every Week-13 day 4–5 of 15. 2026-12-10: 4 of 15, because the last w7-trees rep (d06-mut-copy, weight 2) does not fit. When the current unit is blocked on a failed checkpoint and its dependants are locked, the queue holds a few repairs and variants: 3 of 15 on 2027-01-07/08, 6–9 of 15 on other days. Once those few items are done Today has no next step, the day can never complete, the streak breaks and the week goes off track, so the learner is punished for following Today and for failing a checkpoint. Warm-ups and maintenance add at most 6 more. lib/capacity.test.ts:109-123 only covers queues that still contain light reps.
findings.suggestedFix: When no light candidate remains, accept heavy items up to N. When the course queue runs out, fill from retrieval of ready units within the horizon or from optional sections. If the day still cannot reach N, lower the day's requirement to what Today can actually prescribe, or show the gap explicitly.

findings.title: A checkpoint can be cleared with AI help or by replaying the exact variant that failed
findings.specSection: §2 principles 6, 7; REPS_2_MASTER_SPEC §12 (a different variant after a failure)
findings.evidence: lib/course/credit.ts:77-80 `return (e === 'cold-independent' || e === 'independent' || e === 'retrieval' || e === 'self-corrected') && a.attemptsBeforePass <= 2`; components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:1449-1452 `{phase === 'failed' && (<button ... onClick={explainMistake}>` is not inside `!bare`, and explainMistake (704-726) never calls countHint; app/api/coach/diagnose/route.ts asks for 'the exact line/construct'; rep-workspace.tsx:731-732 the workspace's own repair panel after REPAIR_AFTER=2 has no checkpoint exclusion, and 742-748 `resume: here` returns to the same variant; rep-workspace.tsx:1471-1479 Another/Easier/Harder rep are available on checkpoints; routing.ts:86-88 a later clean pass of a previously failed variant counts
findings.detail: On a cold checkpoint the learner can fail once, have the AI name the faulty line, fix it and pass. That is recorded as 'self-corrected', which counts as gate-clean and as coldEvidence. After 2 failed runs, the workspace offers its own repair set (different from gateStatus.repair) and sends the learner back to the same variant. A fresh attempt there passes as independent and counts, so the exact failed checkpoint is replayed even though gateStatus keeps it out of the queue.
findings.suggestedFix: On checkpoint reps, hide Explain mistake, Another/Easier/Harder rep and the workspace repair panel, or record them as assistance. In gateStatus, do not count a clean pass of a variant that has an earlier failed try until the other variants are used up.

findings.title: Daily completion only counts reps: a prescribed checkpoint or repair can stay undone at 'Day complete', then disappears or appears as 'Bonus'
findings.specSection: §7 one authoritative completion contract; §3; §29 daily completion and Today visibility
findings.evidence: components/course/course-today.tsx:68 `const complete = day.type === 'training' && done >= target`; lib/today-plan.ts:164 `complete: repsDone >= N`; course-today.tsx:252 `{!complete && plan.items.length > 0 && (` hides the list; course-today.tsx:332-334 `Bonus: {plan.optional.find((o) => o.exerciseId)!.title}`; use-today-plan.ts:65 `required` only bypasses the 30% cap; components/course/course-cards.tsx:76-82 checkpoint rows are plain text
findings.detail: Any qualifying credits, including other reps and logged outside LeetCode problems, complete the day while the prescribed checkpoint or repair is still undone. The training list is then hidden, and a checkpoint at the head of the queue that was not yet taken into today's items is offered through the ghost 'Bonus:' button. `required` is never consulted for completion. WeekCard lists the calendar week's checkpoints as plain text with no link, often for locked units, so a required checkpoint cannot be started from Today unless the queue has reached it.
findings.suggestedFix: Make complete mean N credits AND every required item prescribed today done. Keep unfinished required items visible in the complete state and never call them Bonus. Link checkpoint rows to their next variant, or to 'locked until X'.

findings.title: Attempts from before the course decide gates: no recency or cold requirement, gates already cleared on day 1, and any old attempt turns off placement
findings.evidence: routing.ts:83 `const tries = ctx.attempts.filter((a) => gate.pool.includes(a.exerciseId) && (a.completedAt || a.attemptsBeforePass > 0))` has no date bound; credit.ts:79 accepts 'independent' (not cold); data/course/gates.ts:42 `pool: ['o2-cold-letter-counts', 'o2-cold-tally', ...]` and the October-rep pools at gates.ts:44-73; routing.ts:164 placement requires `!liveGates.some((g) => g.attempted)`
findings.detail: For a learner with all October content passed: 14 gates (g-hashing, g-pointer-mechanics, g-fixed-window, g-variable-window, g-stack, g-search-invariant, g-safe-rewiring, g-tree-contract, g-grid, g-graph-traversal, g-heap, g-backtracking, g-dp, g-matrix) are cleared on Oct 26, and 14 units are ready with no course checkpoint. A pass from 86 days earlier still clears (unit shows 'maintenance'). Three first-exposure passes clear g-hashing. The reverse also happens: with 2 of 3 g-hashing variants passed in October the unit is 'practicing' rather than placement, and the last variant waits behind 52 focused path reps. A failed October attempt starts the course 'gate-blocked' with repairs.
findings.suggestedFix: Count toward clearing or failing only gate tries made in checkpoint conditions (on or after COURSE_START, or within a recency window, cold). Treat older passes as prior evidence that triggers placement.

findings.title: Frontier/horizon: an ahead learner pulls Week 13 into Week 2, and once every unit is ready the queue empties and Today prescribes nothing
findings.evidence: routing.ts:206-207 `const frontier = statuses.find((s) => s.state !== 'ready' && s.state !== 'maintenance')` / `const horizon = (frontier?.unit.week ?? 14) + 1`; routing.ts:216-225 ready and maintenance units contribute only LC targets; course-today.tsx:327 `focusConcepts[0] && !week.unlabeled` uses the calendar week
findings.detail: In the simulation with all October content passed, the frontier reached w13-transfer on 2026-11-05 (calendar week 2) and the unlabeled transfer bank was served from Week 2 (3–5 a day). Because unlabeled mode is keyed to the calendar, those items also get 'Review a concept' links. From 2026-12-02 the queue was empty and Today showed 0 of 15 on every training day until Jan 31. Units in maintenance generate no course work.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open Week 13 and Week 14 units before their calendar week or readiness grade. When the frontier passes the calendar, fill from retrieval of ready units or stretch/optional sections. Key unlabeled mode to the item's unit, not the calendar.

findings.title: Repair reps passed earlier the same day show as done but are still pending, so the failed checkpoint cannot be retried until tomorrow
findings.evidence: routing.ts:100 `const fresh = (id: string) => ctx.attempts.some((a) => ... && time(a) > time(last))`; routing.ts:221 `if (!g.repair.length) for (const id of g.next) ...`; lib/today-plan.ts:109 `const done = new Map(all.filter((c) => doneKeys.has(c.key))...` and :118 `open` excludes done keys
findings.detail: Repairs are the 3 easiest unit reps for the broken skills, usually reps passed that morning on the path. Reproduced: g-loop-control fails after the morning path, giving repairs [c1-loop-fill-scan, c1-loop-dbg-past-end, c1-loop-rebuild-first-negative]. Today lists all three as DONE 'Repair' items, routing still has them pending, and no g-loop-control variant is offered for the rest of the day. In the failure simulation this left days blocked on a checkpoint at 3 of 15.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose repair reps not passed today, or give repair items their own key (for example repair:<gate>:<id>) so they are not merged with reps already done today.

findings.title: Ordinary cold path reps are labelled 'Checkpoint' and marked required
findings.evidence: routing.ts:194 `if (e.repType === 'cold' || e.stage === 'retrieval') return 'gate'`; use-today-plan.ts:65 `required: q.purpose === 'gate' || q.purpose === 'repair'`; course-today.tsx:54 `gate: 'A checkpoint: cold, no lesson panel, no solution. Passing it unlocks what comes next.'`
findings.detail: Path reps that are not gate variants get purpose 'gate': all 10 o11-edges reps (Week 2), the 4 tr-chk-* reps (w12), d9-cold-sort-second-desc and d9-cold-top-words (w10), and the Week-14 cold bank. Today calls them checkpoints and promises they unlock what comes next. The workspace treats them as normal reps with hints and solution, because they have no GATE_OF_EXERCISE entry. `required` lets them bypass the 30% foundation cap (a Week-2 day had 11 'Checkpoint' items).
findings.suggestedFix: Give purpose 'gate' only to queue items that have a gateId; give cold path reps a non-required 'retrieve' or 'prove' purpose.

findings.title: readinessTargets behave exactly like targets; 25 of 48 target entries never surface because passing the in-app capstone counts as solving them
findings.evidence: routing.ts:225 `for (const lc of [...unit.targets, ...(unit.readinessTargets ?? [])])`; data/course/units.ts:33 `/** Targets attempted only once their readiness is clean. */`; components/use-course.ts:21 a capstone pass is added to solvedLc; use-today-plan.ts:64 `ready: Boolean(byLc.get(q.lc)?.ready ?? true)`
findings.detail: LC targets appear only from calendar week 3, after the unit is ready, when the problem is not logged and the Reps capstone has not been passed, and when legacy bridge readiness holds (it defaults to true for 217, 1971 and 547). 25 of 48 entries have their capstone in the path (for example LC 167 via cap-two-sum-ii), so the spec's 'TARGET Two Sum II · Opens after checkpoint' never happens in the normal route. In the beginner simulation, LC 128, 424, 39, 53, 139, 62, 54 and 48 sat unready at the head of the queue for weeks.
findings.suggestedFix: Give readinessTargets a real condition (clean gate clearance plus recent cold evidence, per §44) or remove the field. Decide explicitly whether a capstone pass satisfies the LC target, and show either outcome on Today.

findings.title: The first failed run of a checkpoint already marks the gate failed, although 2 failed runs are allowed
findings.evidence: routing.ts:83 `(a.completedAt || a.attemptsBeforePass > 0)`; routing.ts:94 `const failed = !cleared && Boolean(last) && !gateClean(last, ctx.attempts)`; credit.ts:79 `a.attemptsBeforePass <= 2`
findings.detail: Reproduced: one failed submission on c1-g-countdown-steps, with the attempt still open, gives failed=true, state 'gate-blocked', repairs computed, and the variant removed from the queue. Today swaps the checkpoint for repairs mid-attempt; passing on the next run reverses it.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat an open attempt as failed only once attemptsBeforePass > 2 or when it is abandoned.

findings.title: Repair sets differ from the spec: at most 3, sometimes 1, code only, and the same reps every time
findings.evidence: routing.ts:101 `REPAIR_STAGES.includes(e.stage) && e.kind === 'code' && ...`; routing.ts:103 `.slice(0, 3)`
findings.detail: Each failed variant gets 3 repairs, except g-prefix-suffix on d3-cold-sell-today (1) and g-dp-greedy b and c (2). Failing the output-kind variant c1-g-alias-trace still gets code-only repairs. The 'smallest broken skill' is taken as the variant's skills that the gate checks, not diagnosed from the actual failure, so each failure gets the same 3 reps.
findings.suggestedFix: Guarantee 2–4 repairs (fall back to optional or legacy sections), match the failed variant's kind, and use the failing test or mistakeType to choose the skill.

findings.title: The routing tests cannot catch real-flow failures
findings.evidence: lib/course/routing.test.ts:16 `mastery: {}`; routing.test.ts:19-28 `through()` passes every unit rep and every pool rep; lib/course/content.test.ts:24-28 is titled 'at least two real variants per clean pass' but asserts `real.length >= g.need`
findings.detail: Prior evidence from retrievalSkills never fires in tests, the focused-vs-full mismatch never shows, nothing follows the queue rep by rep, and nothing checks curriculum fit (§29) or Today's candidates (the review leak). 10 gates have a pool smaller than 2×need (g-pointer-movement, g-safe-rewiring, g-fast-slow, g-queue, g-grid, g-graph-traversal, g-directed-cycle, g-intervals, g-dp, g-dp-greedy).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progression test with computeAllMastery that follows the queue, a weekly fit test, and a Today-candidates test. Make the content test assert 2×need or rename it.

findings.title: Today's unit focus and learn-first come from course.current, not from today's items; foundation rules follow the calendar week
findings.evidence: components/use-course.ts:23 `const current = statuses.find((s) => !s.locked && s.state !== 'ready' && s.state !== 'maintenance')`; course-today.tsx:96, 101; components/use-course-day.ts:30 weekGates filtered by `s.unit.week === week.number`; lib/course/capacity.ts:11-16 phaseOfWeek uses the calendar week
findings.detail: During the deadlock, the heading reads 'State and while loops' while every item is a hashing rep. Placement and focused units show no lesson or worked example. WeekCard checkpoints belong to the calendar week (often locked), not to the unit in progress. A learner still on Week-1 content in calendar week 3 loses the 30% foundation cap and becomes eligible for LC problems.
findings.suggestedFix: Take the focus unit from the first unfinished course item, and key the foundation and LC rules to that unit's week.

findings.title: Gate variants housed in other units' sections are attributed to the wrong unit
findings.evidence: data/course/index.ts:23-25 UNIT_OF_EXERCISE maps every rep in a unit's sections (last one wins); routing.ts:74 filters variants out of paths; routing.ts:227-229 the queue keeps the first occurrence
findings.detail: Examples: d06-cold-digits (g-recursion, w6) maps to w7-trees; o7-c-last-level (g-queue) to w8-grids; o8-cold-build, o8-cold-components and o8-cold-grid-steps to w9-cycles; d05-cold-index-of and d05-cold-first-at-least to w5-linked-lists; d4-cold-* to w4-stacks; d9-cold-kth-smallest and last-rock to w10; d10-cold-letter-subsets and pick-k to w11-dp. Harmless today, because only the Week-13 checks read UNIT_OF_EXERCISE and no rep is in two units, but any new consumer would misattribute these reps.
findings.suggestedFix: Map gate variants to GATE_BY_ID[...].unitId first, and add a test that no rep appears in two units.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I traced the code path end to end and ran the numbers.

1. Credits. lib/course/credit.ts:104-107 gives every logged outside problem with an lc and a result other than 'failed' its own CreditItem, and tags it `evidence: e.result === 'unaided' ? 'outside-unaided' : 'outside-hinted'`. The "Needed help" button sets `'hinted'` (components/leetcode-list.tsx:139-140: `onClick={() => set(i, 'hinted')}` ... `Needed help`). The course Today renders that list as "Outside problems today" (components/course/course-dashboard.tsx:83). A problem logged by hand on /log with "Hinted" (components/solve-log-view.tsx:198) also becomes 'outside-hinted'.

2. Count. components/use-course-day.ts:35-36: `const done = credits.items[today] ?? []` and `const assistedToday = done.filter((c) => c.evidence === 'assisted' || c.evidence === 'reconstructed').length`. Outside credits add to `doneToday: done.length` (line 51) but never to `assistedToday`. 'revealed' and 'failed' never reach the credit list, so 'outside-hinted' is the only help-type evidence the filter misses.

3. Message. components/course/course-today.tsx:73 passes `assistedCount: cd.assistedToday` into `todayLine`. data/course/motivation.ts:164 sends a met target to 'day-complete'. Line 89 then checks `const leaned = (c.assistedCount ?? 0) > done / 2`. If that is false, the message uses the 'celebrate' tone (lines 92-102) and course-today.tsx:200-202 shows it in the hero.

4. Calculation. I ran a throwaway tsx script against the real `dailyCredits` and `todayLine`, then deleted it; the repo is unchanged. The claim's day (4 hinted reps, 5 clean reps, 6 LeetCode logs marked "Needed help") produced doneToday=15, evidence {assisted:4, independent:5, outside-hinted:6}, assistedToday=4, so 4 > 7.5 is false and the tone is 'celebrate'. Counting outside-hinted gives 10 > 7.5, which picks the warm "A lot of today needed help" line. A more realistic day shows the same thing: 3 LeetCode "Needed help" logs, 5 hinted reps and 7 clean reps give assistedToday=5 against 8 real assisted items, and the line still celebrates. A control day with 8 hinted reps and 7 clean reps correctly gets the warm line.

Severity stays minor. The 15/15 count is truthful under the current credit rule. What goes wrong is which affirmation gets picked: a day that mostly needed help is celebrated as if it were clean, which goes against §2.6/§2.12 and §19's "should feel earned" in tone. The bigger truthfulness problem is that "Needed help" LeetCode logs earn full credit at all. That is §10 (credit.ts:107) and a separate, major finding. This one is a downstream symptom.
result.correctedDetail:
The claim is correct, with one small correction to its example text. The celebratory message is not always "You completed 15 meaningful reps". `pick()` chooses one of three 'celebrate' lines using the date as the seed (data/course/motivation.ts:95-101): "Good work today. You completed 15 meaningful reps…", "Day complete. You did the work the plan asked for today…", or "15/15. Another day of evidence, not just study time." I confirmed all three appear on different dates for the claim's day.

Accurate version: components/use-course-day.ts:36 counts only 'assisted' and 'reconstructed' credits as help. Each LeetCode or outside problem logged as "Needed help" or "Hinted" becomes an 'outside-hinted' credit (lib/course/credit.ts:107). That credit adds to doneToday but not to assistedToday. As a result, data/course/motivation.ts:89 (`(c.assistedCount ?? 0) > done / 2`) under-counts help and picks a celebratory day-complete line for days where most of the credits needed help. Examples of 15/15 days:
- 6 LeetCode "Needed help" + 4 hinted reps: real help is 10, the code counts 4.
- 3 LeetCode "Needed help" + 5 hinted reps: real help is 8, the code counts 5.

Notes for the fix:
- Count 'outside-hinted' as help, preferably through one shared "is assisted" predicate in lib/course/credit.ts rather than an inline filter. That way it keeps working once the §10 outside evidence model (hint, solution viewed, rebuilt) arrives.
- The 'leaned' line promises that "the next session starts with a short repair". For LeetCode, only re-solves that needed help get a redo on the next training day (lib/course/resolves.ts:38 skips 'new' kinds). A first solve that needed help does not, so that copy may need adjusting when outside help is counted.
- This is a symptom of the major §10 issue: "Needed help" LeetCode logs earn full daily credit at all.

result.reasoning:
Every cited line checks out. lib/course/credit.ts:37 `const PRODUCTION = ['code','output','reorder','explain']` and :65 `if (!PRODUCTION.includes(exercise.kind)) return false` mean a choice rep never earns credit. A throwaway script found exactly the 13 choice reps the claim lists in unitReps() paths (W2 w2-hashing x5, W8 w8-queue-bfs x1, W14 w14-interview x7). There are no other non-production reps in any path, and no choice reps in gate pools or optional sections. The 7 W14 reps spread `...R` / `...BIG_O` (data/exercises/oct11.ts:19, :1221; stage 'retrieval', repType 'cold'), so purposeOf (lib/course/routing.ts:194) returns 'gate'. That flows to `required: true` (components/use-today-plan.ts:65) and the label 'Checkpoint' (components/course/course-today.tsx:42, rendered at :288).

I simulated Week 14 Monday (2027-01-25, capacity 15, W1-W13 done). Today lists o11-cx-pop-front and o11-speed-slicing as 'Checkpoint', required. Passing o11-cx-pop-front leaves credits at 0. The item drops out of the queue (routing.ts:218) and out of doneToday (use-today-plan.ts:94-95), and o11-bug-base-case takes the 15th slot. A passed code rep, by contrast, shows a tick and adds 1 credit. No copy on Today or on the rep page says a choice rep does not count.

The claim overstates the W2/W8 part. Those units have gates, so `ready = liveGates.length ? gatesCleared : pathDone` (routing.ts:154). Clearing g-hashing directly gave 'ready' with 0 of 125 path reps passed. priorEvidence also becomes true once 40% of the path is passed (routing.ts:131). The unit then switches to 'placement' (:164) and only gate variants are queued (:212-214); the focused route drops unpassed 'recognize'-stage reps anyway (:157). So only some of the W2/W8 choice reps are ever prescribed. The 'Checkpoint' mislabel is also wider than the 7 choice reps. Severity stays major: the W14 part (and the wider mislabel) materially fails §7 "the daily target and curriculum path must agree" and §4 Q10 "Is there a checkpoint?"; the W2/W8 part is smaller than claimed.
result.correctedDetail:
**What holds:**
- There are 13 choice reps in unit paths, none of which can earn credit (lib/course/credit.ts:37, :65).
- When one is passed it vanishes from Today instead of being ticked, and the next plan item fills its slot. The cause is lib/course/routing.ts:218 plus components/use-today-plan.ts:94-95 with lib/today-plan.ts:114-150. The simulated W14 day showed credits staying at 0/15 after o11-cx-pop-front was passed, with o11-bug-base-case added as the 15th item. No copy anywhere says a choice rep does not count.

**Correction 1 (W2/W8):** "Unit completion requires them" is only true for W14.
- w2-hashing and w8-queue-bfs have gates. Readiness is gate-only (routing.ts:154): clearing g-hashing made the unit ready at 0 of 125 path reps.
- Once 40% of a gated unit's path is passed, priorEvidence (routing.ts:131) switches the unit to 'placement' (:164). The queue then serves only gate variants (:212-214), and the focused route drops unpassed 'recognize'-stage reps (:157).
- Simulated fresh learner working in queue order:
  - w2-hashing switches after 50 of 125 reps. o2-list-literal (#1), o2-set-empty (#15) and o2-drev-crash (#37) are prescribed. o2-dl-empty (#69) and o2-dl-crash (#73) never are.
  - w8-queue-bfs switches after 7 of 17 reps. o7-dq-why-not-pop0 (#1) is prescribed.
  - These show as 'Learn' items (stage 'recognize'), not as required.
- So 11 non-counting items are actually prescribed (3 + 1 + 7), and only W14's 7 are strictly required.

- training-state.ts:26 says tracing only shows recognition.
- mastery.ts:15 says "Recognition alone (choice/trace) caps at 55".

- The reps are o11-cx-* and o11-speed-slicing. They get stage 'retrieval' from the `R` and `BIG_O` spreads at data/exercises/oct11.ts:19 and :1221.

- lib/progress.ts:194 makes every stage-'retrieval' rep 'cold', so a clean pass also adds to `cleanCold` and lengthens the freshness window (training-state.ts:48,53).

- mastery.ts has the same blind spot. `RECOGNITION_STAGES` at :63 and :127 is stage-based, so these multiple-choice passes lift `recognitionOnly`, carry the highest mastery weight (1.25 × 1.5 = 1.875) and add to `coldCorrect`. `coldCorrect` feeds `isStrong` (lib/bridges.ts:59-61).

**3. Two related divergences the claim missed.**
- training-state.ts:48,53 defines its own "clean cold" rule, which disagrees with `coldEvidence` in credit.ts:70-74. It counts a pass rebuilt after an earlier revealed solution as clean cold, and it leaves out self-corrected passes. That is a second, independent definition of cold evidence, which §55 forbids.
- lib/schedule.ts:141 has a third list, `PRODUCTION_KINDS = ['code', 'reorder', 'output']`, without 'explain'. It is only used to pick reps for review sessions, so it does not decide what counts.

**Impact.** The effects stay within the session planner's warm-ups, `repPurpose`, `firstExposure` and the mastery internals. Daily credit, week completion and the readiness report's `evidenceSummary` (lib/course/readiness.ts:71, which counts only full problems) are unaffected. Minor is the right severity.

result.correctedDetail:
Mostly correct. Three points need tightening, and one more affected path should be added.

1. **"Never upgrades" overstates it.** Which attempt counts depends on the order of the in-memory Map:
   - **Same session:** a later attempt made in the same session is added after the earlier one, so it never upgrades the result. My simulation through the real `SyncEngine` kept "assisted" in 400 of 400 runs.
   - **After a reload on a device with an IndexedDB cache:** the order is the sort order of the random UUID ids. That is unrelated to time, but it stays the same on later reloads. The stronger attempt is counted only by chance (191 of 400 runs).
   - **New device signed in to Supabase:** the rows arrive sorted by server `updated_at`, ascending, so the result is tied to the earliest-updated pass.
   - So the same history can show different tiles before and after a reload, and on different devices. Nothing implements "keep the strongest evidence".
2. **Sim A and Sim B are confirmed exactly.**
   - Sim A gives assisted 1 in time order and cold 1 in reverse order.
   - In Sim B the attempts classify as revealed, then reconstructed, then retrieval, and every displayed tile is 0, because `revealed` is counted but never shown.
3. **"Rebuilt after a solution is close to always 0" is too strong.** It is 0 in two cases:
   - The rebuild passes in the same attempt as the reveal. That is the flow the UI points to, at rep-workspace.tsx:617-623 and 610-614 together with the "Clear the editor and rebuild" button. That pass is `revealed`.
   - The learner uses Run it back in the same session. The revealed attempt was added first, so it takes the slot.

   It is not 0 when the reveal attempt never passed (abandoned, then a fresh attempt passed). That case gives `reconstructed:1`. It can also be non-zero by chance after a reload.

   The UI copy contradicts the scoring:
   - Line 1196 says "This rep now counts as assisted".
   - Line 1073 says "This pass earns partial credit; the cold re-solve in 3 days is the one that counts".
   - Line 1394 shows "+1 rep" on every pass.

   In practice, a pass made in the same attempt as the reveal is `revealed`. `qualifies()` returns false for it (credit.ts:66), so it earns no daily credit and appears in no readiness tile. The later cold re-solve is also dropped if the revealed pass comes first in the order.
4. **The same ordering problem affects mock gating.** `transferGrade` (readiness.ts:101-107) uses `as.find((a) => a.passed && a.completedAt)`, which is the first pass in array order. `InterviewCard` (course-cards.tsx:139-140) uses that grade to gate mocks.
   - I tested the 48 real `c13-transfer` reps, each with a hinted pass and then a slow clean pass a week later.
   - In time order the grade is red (0 of 48 independent).
   - In reverse order it is green (48 of 48 independent, `freshFull` 12).
   - So under principle 10 (mocks are readiness-gated), the gate can change on reload. Using the first attempt is defensible for transfer, but only if "first" means the earliest in time.
5. **Related §11 violation on the same lines.** readiness.ts:84 sets `coldIndependent: counts['cold-independent'] + counts.independent + counts.retrieval`, and readiness-report.tsx:66 shows it as 'Cold, independent'. §11 forbids exactly that merge.

**Already correct:**
- `masteryEvidence` (credit.ts:49-60) classifies each attempt correctly in isolation.
- `gateStatus` (routing.ts:81-94) sorts tries by time and accepts any clean pass, so gates, and the domain statuses built on them, do upgrade with later clean evidence.
- `recentAssistance` is computed over all recent passes, not just the first per rep.

result.summary:
The Week 13 rep page itself hides well. Bare mode removes Basics, the concept guide, the teach brief, Building toward, the walkthrough, the Hint button and the missing-prereq warning. The Trains chips stay hidden until a pass. All 48 c13 titles and prompts are free of technique words, and none of them carries hints, notes, briefs, problemIds or a complexity field. The problems are around the page, and in whether the evidence it records can be trusted.

1. **Help is recorded as independence.** "Explain mistake" (an AI diagnosis) and the repair detours are never recorded as help. A checkpoint or transfer rep passed after one counts as self-corrected or independent.
2. **Pre-attempt leaks.** The More menu offers Repair Reps, Another/Easier/Harder rep and Interview follow-up before any attempt. Each one exposes the technique.
3. **Week 13 problems are used up early.** The session builders (Skills "Do reps", Today's cold reviews, repair sets) pull c13 reps, and checkpoint variants, long before Week 13. Skills sessions are named after the skill, and that name shows in the rep page breadcrumb.
4. **The transfer grade is not stable.** transferGrade grades whichever pass comes first in array order. That order is random UUID order, so the same history can grade yellow or red. The memorized-risk check therefore does nothing in practice.
5. **The approach note is weak.** It is one optional free-text line. It can be written after coding, it is hidden in Interview mode, and nothing ever reads it.
6. **Week 13 cannot be completed from Today.** Transfer reps weigh 2 load units, so at most 5 fit per day and Today lists at most 11 items against a target of 15. Green is unreachable in Week 13, and the Week 14 unit stays locked until all 48 transfer reps pass.
7. **Week 14 is not readiness-adaptive, and mocks are open to all.** Week 14 work is the same whatever the grade. /interview lets anyone start a mock at any time, and every mock ever completed counts toward READY.
8. **The readiness card and report ignore the transfer grade and mocks.** They contradict the InterviewCard on the same page.

Also found: a leftover check lock from the October plan blocks 601 course reps when they are opened outside a session. Reloading a rep resets its failure count, which gets around the checkpoint rule of at most two failed submissions.

**Motion:** the global reduced-motion rule is solid. But Winston bobs constantly and strolls across Run/Submit on the coding page (at 1024px and wider). He has no awareness of rest, the flame or completion. Some durations fall outside the spec bands, and reduced motion has small gaps.

**Mobile:** the sticky Run/Submit bar does not stick, because its parent panel has overflow-hidden.

E. Week 13 day fill (lib/today-plan.ts prescribe)

MOBILE

findings.title: AI 'Explain mistake' and repair detours are never recorded as assistance, so checkpoints clear and Week 13 transfer counts as independent after AI help
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:1449-1450 `{phase === 'failed' && ( <button ... onClick={explainMistake}` (no bare/checkpoint guard); rep-workspace.tsx:722 `if (a) persist({ ...a, mistakeType: d.category, mistakeNote: d.diagnosis.slice(0, 200), ... })` (hintsUsed untouched); app/api/coach/diagnose/route.ts system prompt asks for a diagnosis 'naming the exact line/construct' plus a missingPrerequisite skill; lib/course/credit.ts:56-58 `if (a.hintsUsed > 0) return 'assisted' … if (a.attemptsBeforePass > 0) return 'self-corrected'`; credit.ts:79 gateClean accepts 'self-corrected'; lib/course/readiness.ts:109 transferGrade accepts 'self-corrected'

The AI coach names the faulty construct and the missing prerequisite skill, and its 'Repair Reps · pattern' button gives more. Only mistakeType and mistakeNote are stored. On the next pass masteryEvidence returns 'self-corrected'. gateClean then counts the variant as clean, and transferGrade counts the problem as independent transfer, which also gates mocks. The repair offer after two failures (planRepair, 1114-1132), which names the skill and runs repair reps, is not recorded either. This is help passing as independence, and it lets checkpoints clear with coaching.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat a diagnosis as help. Set hintsUsed += 1, or add an `aiAssisted` flag, in explainMistake, followUp and startPlannedRepair. Have masteryEvidence return 'assisted' when a.mistakeType is set or the flag is true. While checkpoint or transferWeek is true, hide 'Explain mistake', or make it explicitly end the clean attempt ('opening this counts as help').

findings.title: Week 13 Today cannot fill its 15-rep contract: transfer reps weigh 2 load units, so at most 5 fit per day; green is unreachable in Week 13 and the Week 14 unit stays locked
findings.specSection: §7 daily contract; §8 curriculum math; §24/§25; §29 Week 13/14; principle 13
findings.evidence: lib/today-plan.ts:67 `LOAD_HEADROOM = 1.3`, :80-81 `case 'transfer': return 2`, :120 `const fits = (c) => count < N && (c.units <= 1 || load + c.units + (N - count - 1) <= maxLoad) …`, :171 `if (e.transfer) return 2`; data/course/units.ts:562-565 w13 `sections: ['c13-transfer'], gateIds: []`, :576 w14 `prerequisites: ['w13-transfer']`; lib/course/routing.ts:154 `const ready = liveGates.length ? gatesCleared : pathDone`; lib/course/readiness.ts:111,115 freshFull >= 8 for green; components/course/course-today.tsx:209 CTA only `{!complete && next && (`
findings.detail: Simulated with prescribe(): N=15 gives a load cap of 20. Transfer reps weigh 2 units, so after 5 the formula 2k+2+(15-k-1) exceeds 20. With warm-up and cold candidates Today lists 11 items (3 warm, 5 transfer, 3 cold); with only transfer reps, 5. Re-prescribing after they are done adds nothing. Once those items are done, `next` is undefined, so there is no CTA and the learner sits at 11/15. The day never completes, the flame never blazes, the streak resets, and Week 13 (4 training days, target 60) ends off track for a learner who followed Today exactly. Only t-01..t-20 are reached in Week 13, and they include only 6 fresh-full reps (t-02, 06, 10, 14, 17, 19). Green needs freshFull >= 8, so it is impossible in Week 13 (at most 7 with the optional Saturday). w14-interview unlocks only when all 48 transfer reps pass, but Today reaches at most 45 over Weeks 13–14, so the 'timed singles' week opens late in Week 14 or never. This overlaps the §8 workload audit but is Week 13-specific.
findings.suggestedFix: Weight unlabeled transfer reps as 1 unit in phase 'interview', or raise LOAD_HEADROOM for Weeks 13–14, so 15 items fit. Alternatively size the Week 13 contract to the load and say so. Unlock w14-interview from the transfer grade (green, or yellow after N attempts), not from all 48 passing. Interleave the 12 fresh-full reps early in c13 order. Add a test: a Week 13 day prescribes exactly dailyTarget items and can be completed.

findings.title: Week 13 problems (and checkpoint variants) are served before Week 13 by Skills 'Do reps', Today's cold reviews and repair sets, in sessions named after the skill
findings.specSection: §24 Week 13 transfer safeguards; §29 'Week 13: no technique leakage'
findings.evidence: lib/sessions.ts:52 `const usable = (e) => … && (DAY_OF_EXERCISE[e.id] ?? today) <= today …` and :86 (same filter in buildSkillSession); lib/schedule.ts:167 `(exerciseDay[e.id] ?? today) <= today` in buildReviewSession; components/use-today-plan.ts:79 `const cold = buildReviewSession(dueReviews(reviews), ALL_EXERCISES, DAY_OF_EXERCISE, …)`; components/skill-detail.tsx:34 `createSession(repo, 'weakest', `${skill.name} reps`, ids)`; components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:833 `const crumbTitle = session ? session.title : …`
findings.detail: Course reps have no October-plan day, so `DAY_OF_EXERCISE[id] ?? today` admits every c13 rep, and every gate variant, on any date. Simulated on 2026-10-26 with no history: Skills 'Do reps' includes c13 reps for 48 of 59 skills (e.g. bfs gives c13-t-14 and c13-t-03), and cold-review picks are c13 reps for 26 of 59 skills and gate variants for 10. At Week 12, with every earlier path passed, the figures are 34/59 (Skills), 12/59 (cold review) and 22/59 (repair sets). Opening a c13 rep from Skills shows the breadcrumb '<Skill name> reps', which names the technique before the attempt. Whatever the context, the bank is used up weeks early, so the 'first' pass transferGrade grades happened in a labelled context, not in Week 13. A gate variant passed in such a session also counts toward its checkpoint (gateStatus counts any attempt on a pool rep).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a shared `practicePool` filter that excludes reps where UNIT_OF_EXERCISE is w13-transfer (unless the course week is 13 or later and the rep was already attempted), gate pool reps (GATE_OF_EXERCISE) and lab reps. Use it in buildSkillSession, buildRepairSet and buildReviewSession. Never put c13 reps into sessions titled after a skill.

findings.title: Week 13 'More actions' menu offers pre-attempt technique leaks: Repair Reps, Another/Easier/Harder rep, Interview follow-up
findings.specSection: §24 (hide pattern, skill labels, concept hints before attempt; record assistance)
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:1460-1491 menu rendered regardless of bare; :1481 `<MenuItem onClick={startRepair}>Repair Reps</MenuItem>` and :764 `const weakest = [...ex.skills, ...ex.prerequisites]…` then buildRepairSet; :1471-1479 Another/Easier/Harder, which call :687 `skills: ex.skills.slice(0, 4)`; :1482 `(ex.repType === 'capstone' || ex.repType === 'pattern' || …) && ex.kind === 'code'` gives Interview follow-up via :779 `requestFollowUp({ title, prompt, code })`; the generated rep's page shows :938 `title={`The basics behind this rep: ${primers.map((x) => x.title).join(', ')}…`}` and components/concept-guide.tsx:117 `{concept.title}`
findings.detail:
Before any attempt on a c13 rep, three items leak:
- **Repair Reps** opens a session of reps on the rep's own skills. Those pages show Trains chips and concept guides, and the session returns to the transfer rep.
- **Another / Easier / Harder rep** generates a 'pattern' rep (transfer:true). It is not in the w13 unit, so its page is not bare: the Basics tooltip lists the primer titles, the collapsed concept guide shows the concept name, and the generator's hints are available.
- **Interview follow-up** asks the AI for questions about the problem.

None of these touches the transfer rep's attempt, so a later pass is still 'independent'. The same detours are open on checkpoints (Another rep / Repair Reps right before a cold variant).
findings.suggestedFix: While transferWeek or checkpoint is true, show only 'Show solution (counts as help)' and 'Skip for now' in the menu until the rep is passed or abandoned. If a detour must stay, call ensureAttempt() first and mark the attempt assisted. Pass `hidePattern: true` and the w13 context to generated reps so their pages are bare too.

findings.title: transferGrade grades an arbitrary pass (array order), so the grade is non-deterministic and memorizedRisk is dead or inverted
findings.specSection: §24/§25 (the grade decides Week 14); §11 (later evidence semantics); principle 12
findings.evidence: lib/course/readiness.ts:106 `const first = as.find((a) => a.passed && a.completedAt)`; :109 `… && !(first && memorizedRisk(first, attempts))`; :180 `const solvedBefore = attempts.some((b) => … b.passed && b.date < a.date)`; lib/storage/sync.ts:101-103 `const rows = await this.local.getAll(t) … m.set(r.id, r)` (IndexedDB key order, no sort); lib/sessions.ts:14 attempt ids are `crypto.randomUUID()`; same pattern in readiness.ts:74-79 evidenceSummary (`seen` set)
findings.detail: Attempts arrive in UUID order after a reload, so 'first' is whichever pass happens to sort first. Simulated: 12 reps, each self-corrected on 01-18 and re-solved cold and fast on 01-25. Chronological order gives yellow (12/12 independent). Same data with the re-solves first gives red (0/12): the re-solve classifies as 'retrieval', which is not accepted, and memorizedRisk is true. The grade therefore flips across reloads, and it gates mocks. When 'first' really is the earliest pass, memorizedRisk can never be true, because it needs an earlier-day pass. The protection runs backwards: a c13 problem first solved in Week 5 inside a '<skill> reps' session (previous finding) is graded on that labelled pass. MEMORIZED-RISK, an evidence class in the master spec, is surfaced nowhere.
findings.suggestedFix: Sort each rep's attempts by completedAt or startedAt. Grade the first attempt made in a Week 13 context (course week 13 or later). Flag memorized risk when any earlier attempt on the rep exists, not just an earlier-day pass, and show it on the InterviewCard and the readiness report. Apply the same time-sorting in evidenceSummary.

findings.title: Week 14 is not readiness-adaptive: same work for green, yellow and red; mocks never enter the day or week contract

findings.title: Remounting a rep starts a new attempt, so earlier failures are forgotten: a checkpoint variant failed twice and then passed counts as cold-independent
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:389-393 `if (attemptRef.current) return attemptRef.current … id: newId()` (one row per mount); :745-747 planRepair `createSession(…, { resume: here })` returns to the same rep; lib/course/credit.ts:58 `if (a.attemptsBeforePass > 0) return 'self-corrected'` (this row only), :79 `a.attemptsBeforePass <= 2`; lib/course/routing.ts:86-89 gateStatus counts any clean row
findings.detail: Verified: on c3-g-pointer-a, row A has 2 failed submits; row B is a reload or the in-page 'Do the repair reps' resume, and passes on its first submit. masteryEvidence(B) is cold-independent and gateClean(B) is true, so the variant counts toward clearing the checkpoint. In one mount, 3 failures then a pass gives gateClean false. A reload therefore gets around the 'at most two failed runs' rule and lets a learner clear the same variant they failed, while routing intends 'repair, then a different variant'. Week 13 is affected the same way: fail, take the repair offer (which names the skill), return and pass, and it records 'independent'. Visible-test Runs are never counted as failures, although credit.ts says 'failed runs'.
findings.suggestedFix: In masteryEvidence and gateClean, count failed attempts on the same exercise since the last clean pass: any earlier failed row makes the pass at best 'self-corrected', and gate failures accumulate across rows. After a gate failure, refuse a clean credit on the same variant until a different variant is passed.

findings.title: Winston animates on the coding page: constant idle bob and periodic strolls across the Run/Submit bar
findings.specSection: §21 (no constant bouncing, no animation that distracts during coding); §23
findings.evidence: app/layout.tsx:24 `<WinstonAmbient />` on every route; components/winston-ambient.tsx:85-86 returns null only when perched or on `/demo`; :54 `const target = Math.max(EDGE, h - Math.random() * RANGE)` (RANGE 140, every 14–36 s); components/winston-ambient.css:60-61 `.wa-sprite--idle { animation: wa-idle 1000ms steps(5) infinite; }`; rep-workspace.tsx:1442 action bar reserves only `lg:pr-24` (96px)
findings.detail: At 1024px and wider, on /rep, /lab, /example and /learn, Winston sits fixed at bottom-right (z-index 5) and bobs on a 1s loop forever. Every 14–36 s he walks up to 140px left, reaching about 224px from the right edge. That passes over the Submit and Run buttons, which sit about 112px from the right edge in the same 56–70px band, and he is drawn above the action bar. This is exactly the constant motion during coding the spec rules out. Reduced-motion users are protected.
findings.suggestedFix: In WinstonAmbient, return null (or a static frame with no strolls) when the pathname starts with /rep, /lab, /example or /interview. Replace the infinite idle loop with an occasional short bob, for example 2 cycles every 20–40 s.

findings.title: Proving reps that 'needed help twice' open the full concept guide for free, and the pass records as cold-independent
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:336-337 `const relearn = … needsRelearn(ex.id, attempts)` / `const learnMode = guideMode(ex, { firstExposure: Boolean(teach) || relearn, … })`; data/concepts.ts:302 `if (opts.firstExposure) return 'learn'`, :309 `learn: { open: true, assisted: false }`; components/concept-guide.tsx:107-110 onAssisted only fires on toggle in an assisted mode
findings.detail: For capstones, cold reps, transfer reps outside Week 13 and October-plan mastery checks: after hint-assisted passes on two different days, the next attempt opens with the concept guide fully expanded (mental model, core moves, usual shape), and it is not counted as help. If no hint is used, the pass is classified 'cold-independent', the strongest signal, and flows into the readiness 'Cold, independent' count.
findings.suggestedFix: For proving reps (guideMode would be 'prove'), set the attempt as assisted when the relearn guide is shown open. Alternatively, open it collapsed with 'Open (counts as help)'.

findings.title: Outside Week 13, 'unlabeled' reps still name their technique (Basics tooltip, concept-guide title, walkthrough card)
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:812 unlabeled = transfer|cleanPass|gate|w13|capstone but bare (828) excludes non-W13 transfer and capstones; :938 Basics `title={`The basics behind this rep: ${primers.map((x) => x.title).join(', ')}…`}`; components/concept-guide.tsx:117 collapsed header shows `{concept.title}`; rep-workspace.tsx:1059 capstone walkthrough label; footer :1206 'The skills it trains show once you pass.'
findings.detail: There are 67 bridge transfer reps outside Week 13, all with primers (e.g. o2-dl-lc-group-anagrams: 'Dictionaries, Lists, Sorting and sort keys'). They show the technique before the attempt while the footer says the skills appear only after a pass. The same applies to generated 'pattern' reps reached from Week 13.
findings.suggestedFix: For unlabeled reps, show the Basics button without the primer-title tooltip and render the collapsed guide as 'Concept guide (counts as help)' without its title. Hide the walkthrough label until a failed attempt.

findings.title: Interview-mode toggle undermines checkpoint and Week 13 UI: Hint appears on checkpoints, and the approach note disappears
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:1480 `{interview && <MenuItem onClick={() => (setMoreOpen(false), void nextHint())}>Hint</MenuItem>}`; :961 banner 'Cold: no lesson panel, no hints, no solution.'; :966 `… && !interview && <ApproachNoteField`
findings.detail: 36 gate variants have static hints, and they become reachable by switching to Interview mode. They are counted, so the gate is not cleared, but the checkpoint banner's promise is broken. On Week 13 reps, Interview mode removes the approach note, so nothing is recorded.
findings.suggestedFix: Hide the Hint menu item when checkpoint or transferWeek is true. Render the approach note in all modes.

findings.title: Transfer grade shows a RED verdict with zero evidence
findings.evidence: lib/course/readiness.ts:113-115 `const attempted = byRep.size … : 'red'`; components/course/course-cards.tsx:150-152 `{GRADE[t.grade]}`
findings.detail: On the first day of Week 13 (and in Week 14 if nothing was attempted) the Today InterviewCard shows a RED pill with '0 of 0'. RED is a verdict; with no attempts it is not yet a grade.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a 'not graded yet' state until attempted >= 6, for example 'Grade after 6 unlabeled problems'. Keep mocks closed in that state.

findings.title: Reduced-motion gaps: JS smooth scrolling, an invisible toast, and static spark dots
findings.evidence: components/rep/basics-panel.tsx:27, 113, 153 `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' })`; app/globals.css:896-903 `.pp-toast { animation: pp-toast 2600ms … both }` with `100% { opacity: 0; }` plus :945-947 duration 0; globals.css:929 `.spark {… left: 50%; top: 50%; …}` and :934-937 `.spark { animation: none !important; }` with components/course/training-flame.tsx:32-43 sparks still rendered
findings.detail: JS smooth scroll ignores the CSS media query. With duration 0 the toast jumps to its last keyframe (opacity 0), so reduced-motion users never see the 'Oct 12 complete…' or 'Every rep in the plan is done.' messages. Under reduced motion the five spark spans stay as a static orange dot on the flame while celebrate is true.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `behavior: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth'`. Under reduced motion, show the toast statically and remove it with JS. Don't render sparks when reduced motion is on, or set them to display: none.

findings.title: Some motion durations fall outside the spec bands; ring-sweep is unused
findings.specSection: §21 micro 150–250 ms, progress 300–500 ms, milestone 600–1000 ms
findings.evidence: app/globals.css:86 `--dur-fast: 120ms` (hover/focus transitions at :380, :414, :446, :469); :860 `pp-tip-in 140ms`; :671 `pop-in 260ms`; components/progress-ring.tsx:35 `stroke-dashoffset 520ms`; globals.css:732 `.pp-fill … 560ms`; :930 `.celebrate-in … 500ms` used for 'Day complete' and milestone pill (course-today.tsx:166, 204); :780 `pp-shimmer 1400ms`; :923 `@keyframes ring-sweep` never used
findings.detail: Hover and focus feedback is below the micro floor. The progress rail and ring overshoot 500ms. Milestone moments ('Day complete', the 50/250… pill) use a 500ms rise, below the milestone band. The finale shimmer runs past 1000ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Set --dur-fast to 150ms. Bring pp-fill and the ring to 450ms or less. Add a 700ms celebrate-milestone class for 'Day complete' and the milestone pill. Cap pp-shimmer at 1000ms. Use or delete ring-sweep.

findings.title: Flame state transitions are instant, and most milestone celebrations are not wired
findings.evidence: components/course/training-flame.tsx:27 `<g transform={`translate(24 44) scale(${scale}) …`}>` and :28 fill swap (no transition); course-today.tsx:166 `celebrate-in` re-runs on every visit; data/course/motivation.ts:142 milestone-1 text exists but :171 `MILESTONES = [50, 250, 500, 750, 950]`; no motivate() call sites for 'gate-cleared', 'mock-complete', 'transfer-breakthrough', 'repair-success', 'streak-increment'
findings.detail: UNLIT to EMBER to BURNING to BLAZE jumps size and colour with no transition. Only blaze ignites, once per device per day. 'First training day' can never fire. First clean gate, first independent Medium, first completed week, first mock and READY have no celebration, and no progress-ring fill is used in the course UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Animate scale with a CSS `transition: transform 400ms` on a CSS transform, and cross-fade the inner flame. Add 1 to MILESTONES, or fire 'First training day' separately. Derive first-gate, first-Medium, first-week, first-mock and READY events from attempts and show each once (localStorage flag) with flame and spark treatment.

findings.title: Winston has no state awareness (§23 reactions absent)
findings.evidence: components/winston-ambient.tsx:7-12 'no awareness of progress'; components/winston-perch.tsx:6-11 'no knowledge of progress' and no props besides className; public/winston/winston-sprite.png has 15 frames (idle 0–4, walk 5–14) only
findings.detail: Winston behaves the same on rest days, before the day starts, at 0/15, at blaze and at day complete. There are no sleep, sit or cheer frames to draw on.
findings.suggestedFix:
Add a `mood` prop to WinstonPerch, computed in CourseDashboard from cd.day.type, cd.flame, `complete` and `celebrate`:
- **asleep** (rest day): frame 0, desaturated, no strolls, with a slow 'z' (static under reduced motion).
- **waking** (first Today view of a training day, flag `reps-woke:${today}`): a single 600ms hop.
- **watching** (ember or burning): stand beside the TrainingFlame facing it (--face), with stroll frequency scaled by flame.
- **cheer** (the existing `celebrate`, or week complete / gate cleared): a single 800ms double hop synced with flame-ignite.

Keep him aria-hidden, without text, and off coding routes.

findings.title: Mobile: the sticky Run/Submit bar does not stick, and the confidence rating is hidden
findings.evidence: components/rep/rep-workspace.tsx:1247 `className="rep-in panel flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden"` is the parent of :1442 `max-lg:sticky max-lg:bottom-0 max-lg:z-10` (action bar) and :1382 (success bar); :1409 `hidden … xl:flex` for 'How solid?'
findings.detail: position: sticky resolves against the nearest overflow-hidden ancestor, the non-scrolling panel, so on phones and tablets the Submit bar stays at the panel bottom, often off-screen below the instructions or keyboard. Confidence is never collected below 1280px.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the action bar out of the overflow-hidden panel on small screens (or use overflow: clip, which does not create a scroll container), or make it position: fixed below lg. Show the confidence rating at all widths.

findings.title: No tests cover Week 13 leakage on the rep page or Week 14 mock gating
findings.specSection: §29 'Week 13: no technique leakage', 'Week 14: mock gating still works'
findings.evidence: e2e/course.spec.ts:93 only the checkpoint is cold; lib/course/content.test.ts:37-38 checks titles and prompts only; lib/course/readiness.test.ts:31-39 tests pure transferGrade/mockPolicy only
findings.detail: No test opens a c13 rep, inspects its menu, breadcrumb or session sources, or tries /interview/mock-1 under a red grade. The 'cold' test does not cover Explain mistake or reload behaviour.
findings.suggestedFix:
Add e2e tests:
- Open /rep/c13-t-03 and assert no concept-guide, Basics, Trains, walkthrough or Hint, no skill-named breadcrumb, and that the More menu lacks Repair/Another/Follow-up.
- Assert buildSkillSession and buildReviewSession never return c13 reps before Week 13.
- Assert that with a red grade /interview disables Start, and that with green two mocks are allowed and counted.

Add unit tests: transferGrade is order-independent, and a reload after failures does not give a clean gate pass.

result.reasoning: I confirmed the claim. In lib/course/readiness.ts:147, `const blocked = statuses.filter((s) => s.state === 'gate-blocked').length` counts units, not gates. Line 154 then prints `${blocked} checkpoint(s) not yet cleared.` Here is how a unit gets that state. lib/course/routing.ts:163 sets `else if (anyGateFailed) state = 'gate-blocked'`, which only runs when the unit is not ready. anyGateFailed (routing.ts:146) means some live gate has `failed`. Per routing.ts:94, a gate is `failed` only when it is not cleared and its latest try was not clean: `const failed = !cleared && Boolean(last) && !gateClean(last, ctx.attempts)`. That leaves three gaps. (1) Checkpoints that were never attempted are not counted. (2) Some units have two gates: units.ts:65 `['g-loop-control', 'g-index-scan']`, :220 and :255. If both gates fail, the unit still counts once. (3) If a unit has one gate failed and another gate never tried, the untried one is not counted. So the sentence under-reports how many checkpoints are not yet cleared, and it is really a count of units with a failed checkpoint. domainOf (readiness.ts:55) already counts properly: `gatesLeft = us.flatMap((u) => u.gates.filter((g) => !g.cleared && g.available.length)).length`. So the per-domain why-text is accurate and only the overall why-line is wrong. §11 says explanations must state why each status holds and must not be stronger than the evidence. This wording is understated, not overstated, so minor is the right severity.
result.correctedDetail: readiness.ts:147/154 counts units whose state is 'gate-blocked': not ready, with at least one live gate whose latest attempt failed (routing.ts:94, :163). The text calls that number "checkpoints not yet cleared". It leaves out checkpoints never attempted, and a unit with two failed gates counts once. Three units have two gates (units.ts:65, :220, :255). The wording should say something like "N units blocked at a failed checkpoint", or the code should count failed gates the way domainOf does at readiness.ts:55. Severity: minor.

result.reasoning:
I checked every cited line and the claim holds.
- data/course/units.ts gives `gateIds: []` to w1-state-while (line 50), w1-integration (110), w2-improve (172) and w7-bst (371). Lines 563 and 580 are also empty, but those units are in no readiness domain.
- lib/course/routing.ts:154 says `const ready = liveGates.length ? gatesCleared : pathDone`, so a unit with no gate counts as ready once `pathDone` is true (line 148: `full.every((e) => passed.has(e.id))`).
- `passedIds` (routing.ts:69-71) drops only passes where the solution was viewed (`a.passed && a.completedAt && !a.solutionViewed`). It does not look at `hintsUsed`, so a pass that used hints still counts toward pathDone. Gated units are different: they go through gateStatus/gateClean.
- readiness.ts:48 counts a unit as ready when its state is 'ready' or 'maintenance'. Line 52 then says 'Every checkpoint cleared, cold.' (or 'Every checkpoint cleared; not practised lately…' when stale) as soon as every unit in the domain is ready.
- The domains at readiness.ts:27, 28 and 36 (foundations, decomposition, trees) each contain one of these gateless units. They can therefore claim cold checkpoints for work that never had a checkpoint and may have been passed with hints.
- The same fallback applies to a gated unit whose gate has no available variants: `liveGates` filters on `available.length`.

This breaks the §11 readiness principle 'no stronger language than the evidence supports'. The effect is limited to explanation text in three domains, and the gated units in those domains really were checkpointed, so minor is a fair severity.
result.correctedDetail: The claim is accurate. One addition: the 'stale' wording on the same line (readiness.ts:52, 'Every checkpoint cleared; not practised lately…') overclaims in the same way. The `pathDone` fallback also covers any gated unit whose gates have no available variants (routing.ts:144, 154), not only the four units with no gate.

result.reasoning: The description of lib/course/readiness.test.ts is accurate. Its only tests are track/domains (:12-25), transferGrade, mockPolicy and a single red finalDecision (:31-42), and e2e/course.spec.ts:47 only checks `readiness-card` is visible. No unit or e2e test calls evidenceSummary (lib/course/readiness.ts:71) or memorizedRisk (:178), the code that aggregates evidence for readiness reporting; evidenceSummary is used only in components/use-course-day.ts:39. No test checks lab evidence in readiness, finalDecision ready/ready-with-gaps or overclaim cases, or mock gating at the route/UI level (no e2e mentions mocks). But the claim overstates the gap: lib/course/credit.test.ts does test evidence classification and the reveal-then-upgrade path. It asserts masteryEvidence returns 'independent', 'assisted' (:17-19), 'revealed' (:25), 'reconstructed' for a later rebuild after a reveal (:30, with coldEvidence/gateClean false at :31-32), 'retrieval' once a clean pass follows (:36), and 'cold-independent' and 'self-corrected' (:58-61). So "no tests for the six-way classification", "upgrade from later stronger evidence" and "revealed then reconstructed" are wrong at the per-attempt level. They are only true for the aggregated readiness report. Minor severity is right: this is a test-coverage gap, not a product-truthfulness defect.
result.correctedDetail: Per-attempt evidence classification is tested in lib/course/credit.test.ts:13-65. That covers independent, assisted, revealed, reconstructed, retrieval, cold-independent and self-corrected, plus the revealed -> reconstructed -> retrieval upgrade (:22-37). What is untested is the readiness reporting layer: evidenceSummary (lib/course/readiness.ts:71) has no test, including whether later stronger evidence upgrades the reported buckets. Also untested: lab evidence appearing in readiness, the transfer and interview rows being wired via readiness(..., extra), finalDecision ready/ready-with-gaps/overclaim cases (only one red case at readiness.test.ts:41), and route- or UI-level Week 14 mock gating (no e2e test mentions mocks; e2e/course.spec.ts:47 only checks readiness-card is visible). Severity: minor.

result.reasoning:
The claim is mostly right. One sub-claim is wrong: solve-log entries do reach the readiness track, but only as a count of problems.

What I checked in the code:
- components/use-course-day.ts:39-40 calls `evidenceSummary(attempts, EXERCISE_BY_ID, today)` and then `readiness(course.statuses, finished, ev, today)`. Neither function takes a SolveEntry list (lib/course/readiness.ts:71 and :141).
- Domains come from `courseStatus(ctx)` (lib/course/routing.ts:137). Its `CourseContext` (routing.ts:56-63) holds attempts, mastery, exercises, sections and today. It has no solve-log entries. `solvedLc` is used only by `courseQueue` (routing.ts:204/225) to choose what to queue next. It never changes a unit's state.
- `recentAssistance` (readiness.ts:81-82) counts only in-app attempts. A logged "Needed help" never counts as assistance.
- `transferGrade` (readiness.ts:99) uses attempts only. `finalDecision` (readiness.ts:166-170) uses domains, that grade, and `program.mocks.completed`. The InterviewCard call is at components/course/course-cards.tsx:139-142.
- The evidence panel (components/course/readiness-report.tsx:64-76) reads `r.evidence`, which comes from attempts only.
- `rebuilt` is never read anywhere except its own toggle at components/leetcode-list.tsx:155-156. credit.ts ignores it, and so does readiness.ts.

Where the claim overstates: lib/course/credit.ts:104-108 turns every unaided or hinted solve-log entry (failed ones excluded) into a daily credit (`outside-unaided` / `outside-hinted`). That flows through use-credits.ts:17 into `finished` at use-course-day.ts:34 (`weekProgress(..., credits.byDate).status`). From there it reaches `lastFinishedWeek` in readiness.ts:148-155, which drives the track and the "why" lines. The "Weeks so far" summary (readiness-report.tsx:87/100) also counts these solves in "qualifying problems".

Throwaway scenario, now deleted. Today 2026-11-04, with 45 in-app credits in Week 1:
- No outside solves: Week 1 is 45/50 and "recoverable", and the why list includes "Last week finished short but recoverable."
- Adding 5 logged solves (any result except failed) gives 50/50 "on-track", and that line disappears.
- Hinted, hinted+rebuilt, unaided, and unaided plus later `review1` cold re-solves all produced the same readiness output. The evidence panel stayed at all zeros, the domains did not change, and finalDecision was the same.

So the outside result type and any later cold re-solve change nothing in readiness. Only the count does, and a hinted solve counts the same as an unaided one.

On scope: outside problems are where the course's required target problems and spaced re-solves happen. course-today.tsx:127/223 links them out to LeetCode/NeetCode, and lib/course/resolves.ts schedules the re-solves at +3, +10 and +30 days. The strongest evidence named in §10, and the "later stronger evidence upgrades the report" rule in §11/§29, therefore never apply to them. The UI even says at leetcode-list.tsx:152, "It comes back cold in 3 days: that is the solve that counts", but that re-solve is worth the same +1 as a hinted first solve, and readiness ignores what kind of solve it was. Severity stays major. It is a material §10/§11 failure. It is not critical, because the report's footnote (readiness-report.tsx:77) scopes the evidence to "capstones, checkpoints, unlabeled and interview problems", so the report is not claiming to include LeetCode.
result.correctedDetail:
Readiness reads outside LeetCode solves only as a count of problems, never as evidence. credit.ts:104-108 turns each unaided or hinted solve-log entry into one daily credit. Those credits flow into the weekly totals behind `finished` (use-course-day.ts:34), and from there into `lastFinishedWeek` (readiness.ts:148-155). So outside solves can change the track and its "why" lines, for example "Last week finished short but recoverable". The "Weeks so far" qualifying count includes them too.

What a solve was never reaches readiness:
- **Evidence panel:** `evidenceSummary` (readiness.ts:71) takes attempts only.
- **Assistance check:** `recentAssistance` (readiness.ts:81-82) is attempts only, so a "Needed help" on LeetCode never counts as assistance in the track.
- **Domains:** `courseStatus` (routing.ts:56-63, 137) has no solve-log input.
- **Transfer grade and final decision:** both use attempts only (readiness.ts:99, 166; course-cards.tsx:139-142).
- **`rebuilt` flag:** nothing reads it except its own toggle (leetcode-list.tsx:155).

A scenario run confirmed it. Hinted, rebuilt, unaided and later cold `review1` re-solves all produce the same readiness output, and the evidence panel stays at zero. A hinted solve moves the weekly count exactly as much as an unaided one.

The course's required target problems and their +3/+10/+30-day re-solves happen outside (course-today.tsx:127/223, resolves.ts). So the strongest evidence in §10, a later cold re-solve, is invisible to readiness and can never upgrade it as §11/§29 require. The UI says the opposite at leetcode-list.tsx:152: "It comes back cold in 3 days: that is the solve that counts." The in-app capstone versions of problems (repType 'capstone') do count in `evidenceSummary`. What is missing is the outside solve log.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim, and every cited line checks out. In components/course/course-today.tsx:67-68, `done = cd.doneToday`, which comes from components/use-course-day.ts:35/54 as `(credits.items[today] ?? []).length`. So it counts any credited rep earned today, not today's prescribed items, and `complete = day.type === 'training' && done >= target` looks at nothing else. That one boolean switches to "Day complete / {done} / {target} · You did enough." (166-170). It also hides the CTA (209 `{!complete && next && (`), the learn-first panel and the item list (252), and it turns on the celebration in localStorage plus the flame. lib/today-plan.ts:164 does the same independently with `complete: repsDone >= N`. data/course/motivation.ts:164 uses the same rep-only test for the 'day-complete' celebrate line.

The routing claim is also correct. components/use-today-plan.ts:60-66 puts gate and repair queue items into `plan` with `required: true`. Once repsDone >= N, `fits()` fails because count < N is false, and `window` is empty, so nothing more is taken. The undone required gate or repair is left in `nextPlan` and becomes `lead`/`optional[0]` (today-plan.ts:161-163). Today then shows it as "Tomorrow: X" (311) and "Bonus: X" (332-334). Labs and target problems are never part of the daily test at all.

Related code that agrees: in lib/course/week-status.ts, `todayDone` (66), `daysComplete` (86) and trainingStreak also rest on credits only. This is a direct violation of §7: "Do not show 'DAY COMPLETE 15 / 15' if a required lab or checkpoint is still unfinished". It makes Today untruthful, so critical is the right severity.
result.correctedDetail:
The claim is correct in substance, with two small clarifications.

(1) Checkpoints are not completely hidden. The complete panel still shows a weekly count, "{cd.gatesCleared} of {cd.weekGates.length} checkpoints cleared" (course-today.tsx:300-302), but only as a minor caption under a "Day complete" headline. It is not a block on completion.

(2) Week completion is partly aware of labs and checkpoints. weekProgress (lib/course/week-status.ts:75-78) downgrades a finished week from 'on-track' to 'recoverable' when required labs or gates are missing. But this applies only after the week has ended; it does not cover target problems, and the per-day `todayDone`/`daysComplete`/streak values (66, 86) still use rep credits only.

The Week-3 "every day Mon-Fri shows Day complete" scenario holds only if the learner earns the full daily credit count each day. Under that condition it is accurate.
